- Start with a daily budget of 20 to 30 USD and scale up the campaigns that are profitable while cutting the ones that are not. (Older, 2019) [L0356.046]
- Start Google Shopping with a daily budget of 20 to 30 USD. The usual starting range is 20 to 30 USD per day when the budget allows. (Older, 2019) [L0356.064]
- Start Google Shopping at $20 to $30 per day. This allows enough daily data to make informed optimizations every 2 weeks without overspending. (Older, 2022) [L0249.055]
- Plan for a minimum of USD 20 per day in marketing spend when starting, mainly on Google Ads through the Google Search Network. Spending less is possible but not recommended. (Older, 2021 to 2022) [L0438.009]
- Start paid traffic for a newly launched product at a small daily budget, around 10 USD per day. Increase spend only on products that prove profitable with a strong MAP-to-wholesale spread and good conversion. (2025) [L0966.108]
- Launch Google Shopping with a small test budget of about $10 per day and keep it unchanged until it is profitable, so the account collects data on which products get clicks and sales. (2025) [L0667.001]
- With two verified suppliers and about 50 products, small test budgets can be run to get the products approved and see traffic, while sourcing continues in the background. (Older, 2021) [L0671.035]

**Maximum starting budgets**

- A maximum starting daily budget of about $30 is suggested for Google campaigns, and smaller starts are acceptable. (2024) [L0360.035]
- For a new Google Shopping account, cap the daily budget at about 30 per day; 50 per day is too high early on. (Older, 2021) [L0247.048]
- In the 2021 Google Shopping setup described, a new account should start with a maximum shared daily budget of about 30 per day, and 50 per day is considered too high for a store with a small uploaded catalog. The catalog should first be expanded so Google has more products to optimize across. (Older, 2021) [L0247.123]
- Start Google Shopping with a $30 per day budget, with the option to start at $10 per day when money is tight. Budgets for Google Shopping and Meta remarketing together came to about $30 to $35 per day in 2023. The minimum target ROAS stayed at 10X. (2023) [L0804.067]
- Do not set a Google Ads daily budget far below $10 per day, because campaigns need enough budget to spend and collect data. The usual starting point is about $30 per day, and $10 per day is the lowest reasonable start. (2023) [L0804.109]
- Ignore Google's suggested budget increases, such as a recommended $90 per day, because those suggestions aim to increase your spend. Set budgets based on your own sales data. (2026) [L0808.030]

**Starting formula**

- Starting daily ad budget = $15 (bestseller shared budget for Google alpha and beta) + $5 (everything-else shared budget for Google alpha and beta) + $5 (Meta remarketing) = $25 per day. Microsoft and Bing are excluded from the starting budget. (2024) [L0360.033]

**Beginner launch sequence (2019 example)**

- Starting budget of $200 consists of the $100 credit plus $100 of the store owner's own money. The 2019 credit for new Shopify stores was $100. (Older, 2019) [L1002.041]

| Channel | Budget | Setting |
|---|---|---|
| Google Shopping (product listing ads) | $180 | $20 per day, running about 9 days |
| Facebook remarketing (dynamic product ads) | $20 | $5 per day, retargeting visitors who came from Google |

The call estimated total spend at about $215, and the budget is spread over several days so Google has time to collect data. (Older, 2019) [L1002.042]

**Procedure (2019)**

1. Finish setting up and optimizing the store before spending on ads.
2. Set the Google Shopping daily budget to $20 instead of $30 to $50, so the budget lasts about nine days.
3. Do not spend the whole budget on day one; allow several days of data.
4. Set a Facebook remarketing campaign with a simple dynamic product ad group at $5 per day, retargeting people who came from Google.
5. Start the daily audit process from day one. [L1002.043]

**Procedure (Source C, undated)**

1. Start a Google Shopping campaign.
2. Set a daily budget of $25 to $50 when working with a starting budget of $500 to $1,500.
3. Set a target ROAS of 3x to 4x, for example aiming for $200 in sales from $50 of spend.
4. Let the products appear in Shopping; no extra campaign structure is needed at the start. [L1508.006]

Source conflict: the Source C procedure above uses $25 to $50 per day with a $500 to $1,500 starting budget, while the Source A sources use $5 to $30 per day for new stores. Both are given because they describe different starting budgets.

### Monthly Caps and Test Budgets

- A starting Google Ads budget of about $1,000 per month is typical. This equals approximately $33 per day. [L0059.001]
- A recommended starting budget for a new Shopping (PPC) account is at least $1,000 per month, which equals $33 per day. [L1341.008]
- A first Google Ads budget of about $500 to $1,000 per month is reasonable. Sales should show within a few days if the campaign is set up correctly. (Older, 2020) [L0967.081]
- A new store can start with about $500 to $1,000 per month in ads, which works out to roughly $15 to $35 per day. Spending above that level should come from reinvested store profit. (Older, 2020) [L0468.187]
- A $1,000 first month is based on a $30 per day Google Shopping budget. Starting at $10 per day is fine but gives slower data. (2023) [L0804.068]
- A first month test budget of about 1,000 dollars can be spent as 30 dollars per day on Google Shopping shared between alpha and beta, 3 to 5 dollars per day on Google remarketing and 3 to 5 dollars per day on Facebook remarketing, then scaled once conversions appear. (Older, 2022) [L1113.056]
- With a $3,000 monthly budget, $2,700 goes to Google Shopping. The remaining $300 goes to remarketing, split into $200 per month for Facebook dynamic product ads and $100 per month for Google remarketing. (Older, 2022) [L0854.041]
- With a total ad budget of 100 USD, put about 90 USD into Google Ads and about 10 USD into Facebook dynamic remarketing. (Older, 2020) [L0961.064]
- Budget split between channels: about 90% of advertising budget goes to Google Ads, and about 10% goes to Facebook remarketing to bring people back to the store. (Older, 2021) [L1090.091]
- Alpha and Beta test split (2019 example): Alpha campaign (high-priority, high-bid, converting keywords) set to $30 daily budget. Beta campaign (high-priority, low-bid, weak keywords) set to $17 daily budget. (Older, 2019) [L0243.014]
- A $25 Google budget can be split so that each of the alpha and beta campaigns gets $12.50. (2024) [L0360.035]
- Daily Google Ads budget is roughly the monthly budget divided by 30. A starting budget of $1,000 per month equals about $33 per day. (Older, 2019) [L0663.006]
- Adjust the starting budget to the cost per click; see the cost-per-click rule under Expected Clicks and Conversions. [L1341.009]

### Scaling Rules

- Start Google Ads with small budgets and optimize every two weeks. Starting with large budgets and letting campaigns run without tweaks is what causes thousands of dollars to be spent with zero conversions. (2024) [L0666.037]
- Start Google Shopping campaigns with small initial budgets. Scale spending upward only as performance data proves profitability. [L0163.008]
- Buy data first: the starting budget is for collecting data on which products get clicks and sales, not for scaling. [L1090.090]
- *(Older, 2021)* Starting with a small budget is for collecting data: impressions, clicks and purchases show which products people find and buy. Use that data to add negatives and adjust cost per click per product, then increase budget once return on ad spend improves a few days after optimizing. [L1090.090]
- Scale the budget gradually with ROAS above 10x, and only as profitable campaigns prove the ratio. [L0270.009]
- Products with a strong MAP-to-wholesale spread and good conversion are the only ones that should receive increased spend. [L0966.108]
- The scaling procedure for Google Ads budgets is:
  1. Set a target ROAS for the current budget, for example 15x on $2,000 spend.
  2. Improve efficiency until that target holds.
  3. Only then scale the budget, expecting ROAS to fall somewhat as spend grows. (Older, 2020) [L1111.112]
- Increase the budget as long as ROAS holds; the ratio is the signal to raise spend. [L1090.092]
- Add money in steps: after the first 2 to 4 weeks of learning, judge the campaign on the data and do not scale on day one. [L0808.029]
- The learning phase for the ROAS target is the first two to three weeks of a campaign. [L0472.005]
- Use the 2019 approach: scale up the campaigns that are profitable while cutting the ones that are not. [L0356.046]
- Keep the test budget unchanged until it is profitable, apply the Google Ads optimizations, and only then scale the budget by reinvesting profits from existing sales. (2025) [L0667.001]
- Scale spending for a product only after it proves profitable and reinvest store profits into ads once the free credits are used. [L0468.121]
- The budget for the second half of the first month is raised only after conversions appear, not before. (Older, 2022) [L1113.056]
- Budget can increase with a profitable ROAS, with no upward limit set in the 2023 source. [L0274.009]

### Ad Credits and Promotional Vouchers

**Credit and voucher offers**

- Google Ads and Microsoft Ads offer discount codes for new advertiser accounts. When first setting up advertising, ask about or search for promotional codes to reduce your initial ad spend. (2024) [L0253.056]
- Use Google Ads vouchers, which provide free credit to start. (Older, 2022) [L0854.038]
- When creating a Google Ads account, select Offer A to spend $500 and receive a $500 credit. No money is lost if spending does not reach $500. [L0184.002]
- Google Ads promotional offers come as coupon codes, either a fixed dollar credit or a matching offer. Matching offers change over time, so check the current terms before signing up. [L0717.003]
- A current matching offer in the US pays back spend up to $150, but only if the spend happens within the first 30 days after the Google Ads account is created. Verify the exact amount and window in the offer terms shown at the bottom of the coupon page. [L0717.004]
- The matching offer window of 30 days starts when the Google Ads account is created, not when the coupon code is received. Create the account only when the spend for the next 30 days is ready. [L0717.017]
- Google's sign-up promotion for new Google Ads accounts (as shown in 2020s lessons, may change): spend $500 within the first 60 days to receive $500 in free advertising credit. Higher tiers of $1,000 and $1,500 spend are unrealistic for a beginner budget, so the lowest tier is the sensible choice. [L0718.002]
- The 2024 offers are: a Google Ads credit of $1,000 after $1,500 in ad spend, and a Microsoft Ads credit of $500 after $500 in spend, with both requiring spending by November 30. [L0360.044]
- The Google Ads credit offer ($500 credit for $500 spend in 60 days) and the Bing offer ($500 credit for $250 spend) together can add up to $750 in free ad credit. This justifies spending at least the required amount during the launch window. (2024) [L0971.061]
- Source conflict on the Microsoft or Bing credit: one 2024 source gives $500 after $500 in spend (L0360.044), and another gives $500 after $250 in spend (L0971.061). Use the terms shown in the offer itself. [L0360.044, L0971.061]
- Source conflict on the Google credit window: the same $500 for $500 offer is described with a 60-day window (L0718.002, L0971.061), while the matching offer described in L0717.004 has a 30-day window. Check which offer type is shown. [L0718.002, L0971.061, L0717.004]
- *(Older, 2020)* Google, Bing and Facebook ad credits offered at signup were worth about $200 to $300 in total for a new store. These are 2020 offers, so check current offers before relying on them. [L0468.120]
- *(Older, 2020)* After the free ad credits are used, set aside a couple hundred dollars for ads and then reinvest store profits into ads. [L0468.121]

### Bonus Offers and Conversion Cost

- A bonus gift can lower advertising cost, not only raise sales. When the bonus removes the reason to compare prices, buyers purchase on their first visit instead of leaving, searching again and clicking a paid ad a second time, so the cost per sale falls. [L1293.036]
- You pay for every click in Google Ads, including clicks from visitors who never buy. Irrelevant or poorly matched traffic therefore costs money with no sales in return. (Older, 2021 to 2022) [L1228.003]
- Irrelevant and wasted spend is reduced by excluding unprofitable products and by adding negatives after data is collected. [L0748.019, L1090.090]

#### Further details

- In Google Ads, the ad for a niche with a higher ad spend should show roughly 1,100 sessions for about 300 dollars per day; the question to ask is whether the traffic converts into sales, not just whether the clicks are high. [L0964.068]

## Pre-Launch Compliance and Store Readiness

### Why Compliance Comes First

- Google's automated crawlers, not human reviewers, scan the site and flag missing or incomplete elements. Make the store fully compliant before creating the Google Merchant Center and Google Ads accounts. Fixing these issues first helps avoid suspensions, review loops and back-and-forth with Google. [L0167.001, L0724.001]
- The crawler checks the store before Merchant Center and Google Ads accounts are approved, so the site must be complete, error-free and free of placeholders at submission. [L0167.001, L0724.001]
- Google crawls the site during setup. Do not proceed if the store has demo products, policies with placeholder text, or any broken links or pages. [L0181.002]

### Compliance Checklist Sequence

Work in this order before any account or campaign is created:

1. Add every required policy and store element to the site. [L0665.131]
2. Confirm the checklist is complete. [L0665.131]
3. Only then set up and launch the campaigns. This reduces the risk of a Merchant Center or account suspension. [L0665.131]

Timing rules that apply to the checklist:

- Complete the Compliance Checklist lesson before creating a Google Merchant Center account. [L0181.002]
- Before setting up Google Merchant Center, Google Ads or a Facebook account, complete the compliance checklist. Following it reduces the chance that the store gets flagged for misrepresentation. (2022, older) [L0803.047]
- Run through the store compliance checklist before submitting products to Google Merchant Center. It covers the required pages and elements to add to the store. (2023) [L0934.071]
- Do not start paid traffic (Shopping, Facebook) before the compliance checklist is completed. (2022, older) [L0969.103]
- The checklist is Module 6, Lesson 6.0.2, "Compliance Checklist", which outlines all requirements to complete before turning on Google Ads live. Follow it to reduce the risk of account suspension. (2022, older) [L0272.035]
- Complete the compliance checklist from the traffic module before launching Google Ads. Run Google Ads alone until sales come in before adding other traffic sources. (2023) [L0804.077]

### Required Store Elements

#### Contact Page

- The contact page must offer at least three ways to reach you: an email address, a contact form and a phone number. (2021, older) [L0671.068]
- Keep the prices, contact details and page content on your site consistent with your ads. Do not let them disagree. Inconsistencies between ads and webpages are a common cause of account reviews. (2021, older) [L0671.071, L0671.208]

#### Policies

- Shopify's policy generators insert placeholder text into refund, privacy, terms and shipping policies. Google treats leftover placeholders as a sign of an incomplete store. Read each generated policy line by line and replace every placeholder before submission. [L0724.025]
- Merchant Center policy details, such as return and privacy policies, can start with the default text provided by the store and be edited later. The store and Merchant Center must eventually match. (2020, older) [L0664.062]
- Before submission, the policies must be final, not default text. [L0724.001, L0724.025, L0181.002]
- Review the compliance section several times before launch. Merchant Center suspensions can come from broken links on the store, filler text such as lorem ipsum, a missing shipping or return policy, or policies entered in Merchant Center that do not match the site. [L0966.083]
- Check that all legal pages are in place and that shipping times are stated correctly before starting Google Ads. New merchant accounts are often suspended for missing legal pages or incorrect shipping times. (Source C) [L0788.024]

Policy requirements at a glance:

| Policy or element | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy policy | Must disclose that the store uses retargeting. A policy that omits retargeting does not meet the Google Ads requirement. | L0421.005 |
| Shipping policy | Must state the exact shipping cost, so customers know what they will pay before checkout. If the header or site promises free shipping, the shipping policy must also state free shipping. | L0724.021 |
| Shipping policy, freight | Freight charges must be disclosed, even if competitors do not show them. | L0360.047 |
| Return policy | Place a summary table at the top. Google crawlers can pull shipping and return data easily from tables, so it helps Merchant Center read the terms. Use clear, specific language. Vague wording commonly triggers Merchant Center flags. | L0724.020 |
| Refund, privacy, terms, shipping | Every placeholder replaced. | L0724.025 |
| All legal pages | In place before Google Ads starts. | L0788.024 |

### Shipping, Prices and Checkout Consistency

- Shipping fees, business name, phone number and tax information in Merchant Center must exactly match the store's website and Shopify settings. Google's bots test the checkout. A mismatch, such as a store charging paid shipping while Merchant Center shows free shipping, leads to suspension. (2021-22, older) [L0727.003]
- Do not mark products as free shipping on Google Shopping while shipping is charged at checkout. This is a compliance problem. (2024) [L0360.047]
- Website prices must match the prices submitted to Google Merchant Center exactly. A mismatch is one of the most common causes of a suspension. (2021, older) [L0671.067, L0671.204]
- If prices, taxes or shipping shown at checkout differ from those in the ads and feed, Google can suspend the entire product feed. Google compares these during checkout. (2021-22, older) [L1170.039]
- Set up Shopify Markets per country so checkout runs in each buyer's local currency. A shopper from the UK or Australia will not easily buy when prices show in USD. (Source C) [L1315.001]
- Create shipping profiles per country, or one international profile with free tracked shipping. (Source C) [L1315.001]
- Showing estimated delivery days in the shipping text is optional, and operators are split on it. It works for some stores and not for others, so test it rather than assume. (Source C) [L1315.002]

### Demo Products, Dummy Stores and Broken Links

- Do not start the Merchant Center setup until the store's compliance requirements are fixed, including removing demo products. Unresolved compliance issues will cause problems with the account. [L0729.003]
- Do not link Google Ads or other ad accounts while the store has only dummy products, because it can hurt account approval. Add real products first. (2021, older) [L0968.063]
- Do not proceed if the store has demo products, placeholder policies or broken links or pages. [L0181.002]

### Business Information and Addresses

- Do not hide business information, such as an address, with text that matches the background colour. Google can treat this as misrepresentation, which can lead to account bans. (2026) [L0808.027]
- Some sellers report that Google flags virtual mailbox addresses as business addresses in Merchant Center. This is anecdotal and not confirmed, so check your Merchant Center before relying on a virtual address. (2026) [L0808.028]

### Reviews and Ratings

- Enabling customer reviews and product ratings in Google Merchant Center is fine when the reviews come from Judge.me, which transfers them automatically. (2022, older) [L0429.059]
- Do not use reviews copied from other websites on a new store. Google can detect this, and it can lead to account problems. (2021, older) [L0671.070, L0671.207]
- Reviews without dates: a review without a date is still impactful for the product types sold, but showing dates can help customers. (2023) [L0964.070]
- Google Trusted Store badge:
  - It requires Google user ratings, about 50 reviews according to the lesson.
  - It must be requested from Google.
  - Reviews alone are not enough. (2023) [L0470.035]

### Live Store, Products and Stock

- Do not set up Google Ads or other paid ad accounts until live products are on the store. Running ads before that is a red flag for Google. (2023) [L1094.037]
- Do not run ads on a store that is not live. Merchant Center accounts and ads are set up only after real products are on the store and it is ready to take orders. (2020, older) [L1111.109]
- A site that does not take orders is not eligible for Google Shopping. The product feed links to product pages where a customer can check out, and approval would not last. (2021, older) [L0801.058]
- Google Shopping ads must link to live product pages that are in stock. Pause a product when stock is short to prevent wasted spend and poor customer experience. (2020, older) [L1111.114]

#### Products That Are Not Ready

Keep products that are not ready out of the ads and store:

1. Open the product in Shopify.
2. Change its status to draft and save. It will not show in the store or in the ads.
3. When images and descriptions are complete, set the status to active and save. It is then pushed to the Google ad account. [L0857.016]

- Products that are ready for sale but not fully optimised can stay in the shopping campaigns. [L0857.017]
- Products missing images or descriptions should be set to draft. [L0857.017]

#### Launch Structure for Large Supplier Sets

- If many suppliers are approved, upload all their products. Set up alpha and beta with all products included once the product pages are complete. Turn ads on after the products are ready. (2025) [L0972.062]

### Supplier and Product Thresholds Before Paid Traffic

Sources give different supplier minimums. Use the values below and apply the most recent one as the floor.

| Source | Year | Minimum before paid Google ads | Notes | Id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Source A | 2024 | At least two supplier approvals with uploaded products | Keep uploading in the background afterwards. | L0856.030 |
| Source A | 2022 | At least two suppliers approved and their products uploaded | Keep getting approvals with other suppliers in the background. (older) | L0963.022 |
| Source A | 2020 | At least two suppliers on the site | After the first campaign runs, use time to get more suppliers approved and add their products. (older) | L0967.080 |
| Source A | 2021 | One or two approved suppliers can start | Do not start with a supplier count below the target. Keep getting approvals with the remaining suppliers in the niche. (older) | L0962.064 |

- Read together, the 2021 source allows a start with one or two suppliers, while the 2020, 2022 and 2024 sources set two as the minimum. Treat two as the floor and the target supplier count as the goal. [L0856.030, L0963.022, L0967.080, L0962.064]
- Ads should start once at least two suppliers are on the site. [L0967.080]
- Product count: have roughly 20 products uploaded to the store before enabling Google Shopping ads. (2021, older) [L1112.005]
- Both thresholds were stated in the sources. Apply the supplier minimum and the product count together. [L0856.030, L1112.005]

### One Store, One Google Ads Account

- Each unrelated store needs its own Google Ads account, registered with a sales email address on that store's domain and a separate phone number. (2025) [L0837.064]
- Stores that can cross-promote to each other's customers, such as a bounce house store and a trampoline store, can share one account. (2025) [L0837.064]

### Prohibited Products and Restricted Categories

- Google Merchant Center prohibits certain product categories from Google Shopping, including adult products, weapons, vehicles and smoking-related implements. Listing a prohibited product usually leads to suspension, and recovery chances are very low. (2021-22, older) [L0727.007]
- Check a niche against Google's prohibited products list before building the store and campaigns. A product category on that list can get the Google Ads account suspended even when the business is otherwise legitimate. (2019, older) [L1069.088]
- Google Ads does not allow advertising for some product categories. A niche in a prohibited category cannot run paid Google ads. (2019, older) [L0467.074]
- If the core products of a niche cannot be advertised on Google, such as paintball guns, the niche is a strikeout because Google Shopping cannot be used to sell them. Other products in the same niche do not change this result. (2021-22, older) [L0490.008]
- For restricted or specialty product categories, check Google's policy and enable the extra restriction boxes in the Google Ads setup. These limit which audiences see the ads. (2021, older) [L0247.055]
- Google's policy on pop-ups and large sticky ads targets elements that block a visitor from using the page. A sticky top announcement bar or homepage banner that does not block content was not expected to break this rule. (2022, older) [L1281.108]

#### Information Products

- Information products such as courses can only be advertised through Google Shopping and product listing ads if a physical item is shipped with them, for example a workbook. Without a shipped item, the ad account risks being suspended. (2019, older) [L1002.015]

#### Health and Diet Products

- Use factual product attributes, such as low-calorie, gluten-free and seed-oil-free, and lifestyle benefits, such as macro-friendly, diet-friendly and supports low-sugar diets. Avoid absolute health claims or medical assertions. (Source E 2025-26) [L0220.028]
- Be transparent about ingredient variations. For example, some product flavours may use sucralose while others are naturally sweetened. (Source E 2025-26) [L0220.028]
- Google's health policies are strict. Ads making unsupported health claims will be disapproved or suspended. (Source E 2025-26) [L0220.028]

#### Organic Fallback

- Plan organic traffic from SEO and content from the start. A store can grow through organic search even after losing ad access. (2019, older) [L0467.074]

### Ad Consistency

- Do not let the price, contact details or page content on your site disagree with your ads. (2021, older) [L0671.071, L0671.208]
- Merchant Center and the store must eventually match on policies and business details. [L0664.062, L0727.003]

### Readiness Before Any Ad Account Is Opened

Complete these steps in order before creating a Google Merchant Center, Google Ads or other paid ad account:

1. Complete the compliance checklist, including every required page and store element. [L0181.002, L0803.047, L0665.131]
2. Make the store live with real products and the ability to take orders. [L1094.037, L1111.109, L0801.058]
3. Remove demo products, dummy data and placeholder text, and fix broken links. [L0729.003, L0968.063, L0724.025, L0966.083]
4. Publish the contact page with at least three contact methods. [L0671.068]
5. Publish the privacy policy with retargeting disclosed, and the shipping and return policies with exact terms. [L0421.005, L0724.021, L0724.020]
6. Confirm that prices, shipping fees, tax information and business details match in the store, Shopify and Merchant Center. [L0671.067, L0727.003, L1170.039]
7. Confirm that the niche and its core products are not prohibited or restricted, and enable the extra restriction boxes where required. [L0727.007, L1069.088, L0490.008, L0247.055]
8. Confirm the supplier count and product count thresholds are met. [L0856.030, L1112.005]
9. Set products that are not ready to draft, and keep only in-stock, live product pages in the feed. [L0857.016, L0857.017, L1111.114]
10. Link Google Ads only after the store is ready, and run Google Ads alone until sales come in before adding other traffic sources. [L0968.063, L0804.077]

## Setting Up Google Accounts: Ads, Analytics, Search Console, Tag Tracking

### Setup Order and Measurement First

- Build the measurement infrastructure before spending on Google Ads. Sales can only be attributed to specific campaigns, and performance can only be optimised, if that infrastructure exists [L0032.001].
- Complete this setup before spending on Google Ads [L0032.002]:
  1. Link your Google Ads account to Google Analytics.
  2. Configure basic retargeting audiences and verify they are capturing visitor data.
  3. Activate conversion tracking and confirm it is recording purchase transactions. [L0032.002]
- Set up Google Ads, Google Shopping, Google Analytics and Google Merchant Center together from the first day of the store [L0715.021].
- Three components are required before running Google Ads in this approach. All three accounts are free to set up [L0714.010]:
  1. Google Analytics, to track website activity and build audiences of visitors who interacted in certain ways, for remarketing.
  2. Google Merchant Center, where all products are submitted to Google.
  3. Google Ads account, where the actual ad campaigns are created. [L0714.010]
- The same Google Analytics, Merchant Center and Google Ads accounts that enable paid campaigns also provide free Google traffic, so correct setup supports both paid and free Google visibility [L0714.012].
- Google traffic setup, in order [L0393.012]:
  1. Sign up for Google Ads, Google Search Console and Google Merchant Center.
  2. Create your first Google Shopping campaign and your first Google remarketing campaign. [L0393.012]
- Google Search Console and Google Merchant Center are set up alongside Google Ads. Merchant Center supplies the product feed that Google Shopping campaigns use [L0393.013]. Merchant Center feeds product data to Google Shopping campaigns, while Search Console covers search visibility of the store site [L0532.017].
- Traffic setup on Google and Bing, in order (Bing steps are not covered in these units) [L0532.016]:
  1. Sign up for Google Ads, Google Search Console and Google Merchant Center.
  2. Create the first Google Shopping and remarketing campaigns.
  3. Sign up for Bing Ads, Bing Webmaster Tools and Microsoft Merchant Center.
  4. Create the first Bing Shopping campaign. [L0532.016]
- Account count, with a conflict in the sources:
  - A new store typically needs four Google accounts: Google Ads, Google Merchant Center, Google Search Console and Google Analytics [L0857.018].
  - A Shopify store launched with Google Shopping is described as needing four accounts or connections, but the unit lists three: Shopify with Google Analytics, Google Merchant Center and Google Ads. The Google Ads account is the first marketing channel and is focused on Google Shopping [L1065.004].
- Use the build-phase module on Google Ads setup even for an established business if existing campaigns are not performing as expected, so the account setup can be checked and corrected [L1495.003].

### One Google Identity and One Email

- Create a dedicated business Google account email, not your personal primary Gmail [L0358.009].
- Use that same email for Gmail, Google Analytics, Google Search Console (formerly Webmaster Tools), Google Merchant Center and Google Ads, so the properties can link and share data [L0358.009].
- Using the same email for Google Ads, Google Analytics and Google Merchant Center lets the accounts detect each other, which removes manual permissions and reduces setup errors [L0184.006].
- Google links the accounts with one click only when they share one owner email [L0714.011].
- Use the same email for all three accounts (Analytics, Merchant Center, Google Ads) when setting them up in this order [L0714.013]:
  1. Create a Google Analytics account to track website activity and to build visitor audiences for remarketing.
  2. Create a Google Merchant Center account and submit all store products to it.
  3. Create a Google Ads account to build the ad campaigns.
  Use the same email address for all three accounts so Google can link them with one click and let data pass between them. [L0714.013]
- Use the same email for Google Ads, Merchant Center and Google Analytics, because Data Manager then lists the matching accounts automatically when you connect products [L0718.006].
- Use the same Google Workspace email for Merchant Center, Google Analytics and Google Search Console so the platforms can connect. Domain verification is then completed through Search Console automatically [L0729.015].
- Log in to Google Ads with the same Google email used for Search Console and Analytics, so all Google properties stay under one identity [L0717.007]. Using a different address splits the properties across separate identities and makes the setup inconsistent [L0717.016].
- The Google Ads Linked accounts screen and the Analytics Google Ad Links screen only list Google Ads accounts tied to the same Google email as the Analytics account. Use one email for Google Analytics, Search Console and Google Ads [L1520.002].
- Create the Google Ads account by logging in with your Google Workspace email address [L0184.001].
- Create the Merchant Center and Google Ads accounts with the owner's company email as admin, while customer-facing contact details use the store's customer service email [L1088.047].
- If the Google Ads account is created with a different email than Google Analytics, either create a new Google Analytics account or create a new Google Ads account using the Analytics email, depending on how much setup is already done [L0358.011].
- The main email of an existing Google Ads account cannot be changed. You can add another user as admin with full access [L0358.011].

### Creating the Google Ads Account in Expert Mode

- Create the account at ads.google.com [L0027.001].
- Create the Google Ads account first, without building any campaign. Campaign creation comes later, after the account is configured [L0717.001].
- Enter the business name and website, click Next, select Skip wherever possible, and choose Leave campaign creation to avoid Google's forced campaign setup attempt [L0184.003].
- Use the standard sign-up, not AdWords Express, if you plan to optimise campaigns. Express removes most manual control features [L0716.001, L0716.010].
- Google has renamed AdWords to Google Ads and changes its sign-up flow often, so screens may differ. Follow the logic (standard sign-up, control over settings, billing setup) rather than exact button positions [L0716.002]. Both names refer to the same product today [L0726.003].
- Avoid the automated goal-based options offered during sign-up, because they reduce manual control over targeting and websites [L0716.003].
- Do not let the wizard generate AI ads or accept automated AI features during setup. Generated ads are low quality and the automation tends to consume budget quickly [L0718.004].
- Skip the AI-generated ad questions, skip linking additional accounts, skip the goal selection, and choose the option to leave campaign creation [L0718.001].
- Do not build any campaign at account creation. Google will keep prompting you to create a campaign after the account exists. Ignore these prompts until your planning, research and campaign setup are ready [L0716.011, L0716.004].
- Do not use the simple guided Google Ads setup for a high-ticket dropshipping business. Google earns most of its money from ads, so its recommendations may favour Google over your margins. Goals such as getting more calls do not reflect a sound business objective [L0726.018].
- Enter the business address in the Google account used for Google Ads [L0696.015].
- Create a separate Google Ads account for each business. If the login already shows an existing account, choose Create new Google Ads account [L0717.008].
- A new business needs a new Google Ads account. An old account can be left alone or have its campaigns deleted, and the historical data stays [L1092.074].
- If you already have a working Google Ads account, do not repeat the account setup. The account only needs to be created once per business [L0716.012].
- After submitting business information, Google shows a completion message and opens an account with no campaigns. This empty state is expected, and campaigns are added later [L0717.018].
- Once the account is created, leave it without a campaign and mark the setup as complete [L0717.015].
- Log in and start from the Expert Mode wizard. Click Switch to expert mode instead of continuing in easy mode, which asks about the main advertising goal. Then click Create an account without a campaign [L0717.009].
- Standard account creation, step by step [L0716.010]:
  1. Search for Google Ads (or AdWords) and open the sign-up page.
  2. Select the standard sign-up, not AdWords Express.
  3. Skip the first campaign by choosing the option to create a campaign later.
  4. Enter the billing information and select the currency, which cannot be changed later.
  5. Enter the customer info: Individual or Business, and for a business the business name and address.
  6. Choose automatic payments and enter the credit card details.
  7. Submit the payment details.
  8. If the page is stuck on start reaching people, refresh the page and continue the billing setup.
  9. Open the billing settings and confirm that the account, the payment method and the billing details are saved. [L0716.010]
- Expert-mode account creation with the coupon, as one run [L0717.012]:
  1. Go to ads.google.com and open the coupon page for your country.
  2. Enter your email and click Get the offer code. Wait for the code by email (up to one minute).
  3. Sign in to Google Ads with the same email used for Google Search Console and Google Analytics.
  4. Click Switch to expert mode in the setup wizard.
  5. Click Create an account without a campaign.
  6. Enter the billing country, time zone (keep it consistent with other Google properties) and currency.
  7. Click Submit and confirm the account setup is complete.
  8. Later, to redeem the coupon: click the wrench icon (Tools and settings), open Billing and payments, add a payment method, then open Manage promotional codes and enter the code. [L0717.012]
- Full wizard run for a new store before Google Shopping ads [L0718.001]:
  1. Open the account sign-up page via the link provided with the lesson and check which promotional offer is shown, as offers change over time.
  2. Pick the offer that requires the smallest spend (offer A, which gives $500 credit after $500 spend in 60 days) and claim it. If the spend threshold is not reached, nothing is lost apart from the missing credit.
  3. Sign in with the Google Workspace account that will be used for the whole setup.
  4. Enter the business name and the store URL in the wizard and continue.
  5. Skip the AI-generated ad questions, skip linking additional accounts, skip the goal selection, and choose the option to leave campaign creation so no campaign is created.
  6. Confirm billing country, time zone and currency and continue.
  7. Set up the payments profile: choose Individual (or Organization if a company exists, or a proprietor name for sole traders) and add a payment method. A temporary $50 authorisation appears on the card and is usually released within a week or sooner.
  8. Answer no to the offer of personalised guidance from a Google Ads account strategist, then submit to create the account. [L0718.001]
- Account sign-up forces a first campaign. Do not use it. Skipping through the wizard and leaving campaign creation avoids an unwanted campaign that would otherwise have to be switched off [L0718.003].
- After payment, the new interface may stay stuck on a start reaching people screen with an error. Refresh the page and open billing settings to check whether the account and payment method were created, because the account can exist despite the error [L0716.009].
- Verify in billing settings that the account, payment method and billing details are saved [L0716.010].

### Campaign Prompt During Sign-Up: Three Routes

| Route | What you do | When it applies | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Skip the campaign (current recommendation in these units) | Leave campaign creation, use Expert Mode, and choose Create an account without a campaign | Default for a new store; avoids an unwanted campaign | [L0717.009, L0184.003, L0718.001, L0718.003] |
| B. Enter a keyword and pause immediately | On first opening, enter any keyword, then pause that campaign at once | Described as the first-open prompt; the unit does not give a date | [L0027.001] |
| C. Set up a campaign, pause it, and activate after approval (older advice, 2019) | Create the first campaign with a budget, pause it, wait for approval, then activate it when ready to spend | Older approach; also used to read the Google Keyword Tool | [L1068.061, L0243.009] |

- Route C, the older 2019 approach, in full [L1068.061]:
  1. Create the first campaign, which requires setting a budget.
  2. Pause the campaign immediately.
  3. Wait for approval while the account is pending.
  4. Once approved, the paused campaign can be activated when ready to spend. [L1068.061]
- Older 2019 advice on early-stage stores: create the account before the first supplier approval (timing is flexible), set up at least one campaign, turn it off immediately to prevent spending, and use the live account to read keyword search volume and cost-per-click estimates in the Google Keyword Tool without ad spend [L0243.009].
- Do not opt into the personalised guidance from a Google Ads account strategist offered during payment setup. These reps are sales staff who push automated features and higher spend, so answer no [L0718.005].

### Time Zone, Currency and Billing Country

| Setting | Can it be changed later? | Guidance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Billing country | No | Must be the country the business operates in. The coupon page is chosen for the country where the billing address is located. | [L0726.019, L0726.017, L0717.002] |
| Time zone | No | Two guidelines apply together: (a) it determines when your ads run, so choose it based on the hours and region where you want campaigns active; (b) keep it consistent with Search Console and Analytics (for example Eastern), because mismatched time zones make cross-tool reporting harder | [L0027.002, L0027.003, L0717.010, L0717.011] |
| Currency | No | Pick the currency you will pay in. Confirm it is the currency the Shopify store takes payments in | [L0027.002, L0717.010, L0726.017] |

- Time zone and currency are set at account creation and cannot be modified later [L0027.002].
- In the business information step, set the billing country, time zone and currency, then click Submit [L0717.010].
- Billing country, time zone and currency in a new account cannot be changed later. Confirm them carefully before submitting [L0726.019].
- Billing country, time zone and currency must be checked for correctness before continuing, because they are set at account creation [L0718.008].

### Coupons and Promotional Offers

- Use the official coupon page Google publishes for promotional offers. Select the coupon page for the country where the billing address is located [L0717.002].
- Outside the US, search google.com for Google Ads Voucher plus the country name, then open the link that leads to the Google Ads page for that country [L0717.005].
- The coupon page shows offers for the country the visitor is located in. A US visitor sees the US offer. Visitors outside the US should search for Google Ads Voucher plus their country name [L0717.019].
- Enter an email address on the coupon page and click Get the offer code. The code is sent by email within one minute. You can apply it after the account has started [L0717.006].
- To redeem a coupon, click the wrench icon at the top (Tools and settings), then Billing and payments. Set up a payment method first, because the promotional code can only be entered after that. Manage promotional codes appears under the payment setup [L0717.013].
- The coupon can only be applied to the Google Ads account that is linked to the payment method [L0717.014].
- Do not add billing information to an account you will never use, because it only creates unnecessary setup [L0717.014].
- Pick the smallest-spend offer when several are shown (offer A in the source gives $500 credit after $500 spend in 60 days). Offers change, so check the sign-up page each time [L0718.001].

### Payment Method and First Charges

- No money is spent during account setup. The account is created and connected so Google Shopping ads can start once products are approved in free listings. The payment method is only charged after ads run [L0718.009].
- Choose automatic payments and enter the card details [L0716.010].
- A temporary $50 authorisation appears on the card during payment setup and is usually released within a week or sooner [L0718.001].
- In a new Google Ads account, Data Manager only becomes available after a payment method has been entered. Until then the connected-products list is empty, which is normal for a brand-new account [L0718.014].

### Account Approval and Billing Threshold (Older Advice, 2019)

- Google Ads usually bills once the account reaches its billing threshold, which is set in the Google Ads settings and was stated as $500 by default in 2019. Accounts can differ, so check the threshold [L1068.060].
- Approval for a new account usually takes 1 to 3 days. It can sometimes take 24 hours, and occasionally longer [L1068.062].
- Google's sign-up and the first campaign build are described in the Route C steps above, which were written in 2019 [L1068.061].

### Linking Google Analytics (GA4) to Google Ads

- Linking Google Ads to a GA4 property lets the two platforms share data, including audiences. Once linked, audiences built in Google Analytics can be used for Google Ads campaigns [L1520.001].
- Link Google Ads to Google Analytics (GA4) [L1520.003]:
  1. Log in to Google Analytics.
  2. Click the gear icon in the bottom left corner to open Admin.
  3. In the right-hand column, scroll down to Product links and click Google Ad Links.
  4. Click Link.
  5. Select the Google Ads account that is listed (it must use the same email address).
  6. Click Link again.
  7. Check the new link: it shows the Google Ads account name, the account ID, whether personalised advertising is enabled, and who created the link. [L1520.003]
- Older Universal Analytics route (2021-22 source, labelled UA): in Google Ads, open Tools and settings, go to Linked accounts, click Google Analytics (UA), turn Auto-tagging on by clicking Enable, check the Analytics property shown, click Link and switch the toggles to green, then click Save [L0726.021].
- Before linking, make sure the login email in Analytics matches the login email in Google Ads, and that user has Edit access to the property. Otherwise no Analytics property appears for linking [L0726.023].
- An audience built in Google Analytics does not reach Google Ads unless the Google Ads account is selected as an audience destination before saving [L1390.028].
- After linking, data only flows between the two platforms once ads have actually been running. A newly linked account shows little or no shared data until the first campaigns go live [L0726.027].

### Auto-Tagging

- Turn on auto-tagging in Google Ads before linking to Analytics. It makes click data flow into Google Analytics with better detail about ad performance [L0726.022, L0726.021].
- Auto-tagging is switched on with the Enable button in the Google Analytics linked-accounts section of Google Ads (2021-22 Universal Analytics route) [L0726.021].

### Data Manager and Merchant Center Link

- Connect Google Analytics and Merchant Center in Google Ads [L0184.005]:
  1. In Google Ads, navigate to Tools, then Data Manager.
  2. Click Connect product.
  3. Select your existing Google Analytics account and Google Merchant Center account.
  4. Confirm both display as Linked when complete.
- Navigation path: Google Ads, Tools (left navigation), Data Manager, Connect product (blue button), then select Google Analytics and Google Merchant Center. Both must show as linked before moving on [L0718.007].
- Before the Google Ads setup counts as finished, Data Manager must list Google Analytics and Merchant Center as connected, both showing linked. Accounts signed in with the same email appear as selectable options [L0718.015].
- Data Manager is empty in a new account until a payment method is entered [L0718.014].
- Three-step foundation summary before running Google Shopping ads [L0718.013]:
  1. Create the Google Ads account.
  2. Connect Google Analytics and Google Merchant Center to Google Ads via Data Manager, both showing as linked.
  3. In the Shopping feed app, open Tracking Tags, choose Google dynamic remarketing and conversion tracking, link the Google Ads account, and let the app create all tags. [L0718.013]

### Conversion Tracking and Tags via the Google Shopping Feed App

- The app named Symprosis in L0184.007 and L0187.003 is spelled Simprosys in L0718.013. The same app is meant in each case.
- Set up Google tracking for Shopping via the feed app [L0184.007]:
  1. Open the Symprosis Google Shopping Feed app in Shopify.
  2. Hover over Tracking Tags.
  3. Click Google Dynamic Remarketing and Conversion Tracking.
  4. Connect your newly created Google Ads account and approve permissions.
  5. Enable Conversion tracking and Dynamic remarketing.
  6. The app automatically creates, installs and configures tracking tags and Google Ads events. [L0184.007]
- In the Shopify product feed app, open tracking tags, hover over it, then click Google dynamic remarketing and conversion tracking. If the setup was made years ago, an update is probably needed because tracking has changed [L0472.015].
- A Merchant Center message about a conversion measurement problem usually means conversion tracking is missing or outdated. Check the tracking tags in the product feed app and re-run the Google setup before changing campaigns [L0472.016].
- Tracking events (Add to cart, Begin checkout, Purchase) must be pre-installed via the feed app. The Purchase event may appear as Purchase or Purchase in category. Duplicate tags from reinstalling are normal, so select the correct one instead of excluding them [L0187.003].
- Use the Google Shopping feed app (the one used to set up the Google integration) to create conversion tracking events automatically. Do not install a separate Google Ads pixel app [L0964.053, 2023].
- Conversion tags are created through the feed app. Disconnect any tags added by someone else through Google Tag Manager before creating new campaigns [L1116.029].
- If a previous third party paused old campaigns, re-enable them after the correct tags are reinstalled. If they were deleted, rebuild from scratch [L1116.028].
- Only one purchase conversion tag should be primary, and the rest should be secondary. If the purchase tag set up by the feed app is in use, keep it primary, set the others secondary, and avoid running two conflicting tag sets from different apps [L1287.041].
- Conversion tracking for Google is set up through the store's Google sales channel process. A separate tracking tag is not needed if that process already sends conversions [L0855.024, 2023].
- Feed-app tracking tags may initially display as Unverified after setup. This is normal, and they become active once traffic and purchases occur [L0184.008].
- Google's removal of third-party cookies and iOS tracking limits changes how tracking is set up, not whether Google Ads works. Expect the setup to change but Google Ads to keep working [L1090.108, 2021].

### Shopify Without the Feed App: Conversion Pixel Route

Two routes exist in the sources. Use the pixel app route only when no feed app handles the tags. L0964.053 (2023) advises against installing a separate pixel app when the feed app is used.

- Conversion tracking on Shopify no longer requires editing theme code. A conversion-pixel app from the Shopify App Store installs the latest Google Ads pixel automatically. Coding the pixel manually by editing Liquid files is an advanced, optional route that is harder to maintain [L0391.001].
- Install Google Ads conversion tracking on Shopify without code [L0391.002]:
  1. Open the Shopify App Store and search for Google Ads conversion pixel (listed under apps.shopify.com).
  2. Install the app and log in to it.
  3. Link your Google Ads account inside the app. This takes a minute or two.
  4. Confirm in Google Ads under Settings, Measurement, Conversions that a conversion action for the store (purchases) has been created automatically.
  5. Expect the status unverified until the first real conversion arrives. The status then changes to active. [L0391.002]
- In Google Ads, under Settings, Measurement, Conversions, the automatically created Shopify conversion action shows status unverified until the first real purchase is tracked. After that it becomes active and tracks each conversion with a 30-day click-through conversion window [L0391.003].
- The default conversion window is 30 days. A click on day 1 still counts if the purchase happens within the following 30 days, and the conversion is attributed to the original click date [L0391.004].
- A Shopify store without a developer can get Google Ads conversion tracking, the Google Analytics link, enhanced ecommerce and remarketing tags working in roughly 10 minutes using the app and Shopify integration instead of manual code [L0391.015].

### Verifying Tags

- Verify Google Ads and Google Analytics tracking on a Shopify store with Google Tag Assistant [L0391.016]:
  1. Install the Google Tag Assistant browser tool.
  2. Open the live Shopify store in the browser.
  3. Check that the Google Ads remarketing tag is active on the site.
  4. Check that the global site tag is live.
  5. Refresh the page and confirm that the Google Analytics code loads.
  6. If any tag is missing, go back to the app or Shopify Google Analytics settings and recheck the linked IDs before relying on the data. [L0391.016]
- Check tracking status in Google Ads and optionally use Google Tag Assistant to confirm tracking is working [L0234.013].

### Purchase-Only Conversion Signal

- Keep only Purchases as the conversion signal in Google Ads. Remove page views, lead form submissions and all other actions, so Google optimises for buying, not browsing [L0210.003].

### Search Console and Indexing

- Google Search Console is free to set up. It shows impressions, clicks and keywords for your store, so add the store there to see detailed search data [L0801.066, 2021].
- Google Search Central (formerly Google Webmaster Tools) gives detailed reporting on impressions, clicks and keywords. Link your store there to see which search terms bring traffic [L0801.067, 2021].
- Search Console shows whether your website and product pages are indexed in Google organic results, and flags errors that stop Google from reading the site [L0852.069, 2020].
- After setup and verification, Search Console lets products rank organically in Google Search results and brings buyer-intent traffic that grows over time [L0168.001].
- Google Webmaster Tools (older naming, 2020) instructs Google to crawl the website regularly and detect new content, including star reviews. Configure this so rich snippets (star ratings) appear in search results once products receive reviews [L0245.023, 2020].
- Request indexing of new product pages and blog pages in Search Console for faster crawling and indexing [L0249.063, 2022].
- Indexing check, with two numbers in the source [L0274.053, 2023]:
  - If Merchant Center shows 2,000+ non-indexed pages with odd URLs while about 250 indexed pages are normal, the non-indexed pages are variants or images.
  - If 250 normal URLs are indexed, the store is fine. No action is needed.
- Use the same Google Workspace email for Search Console, Merchant Center and Google Analytics. Domain verification is then completed through Search Console automatically [L0729.015].

### Call Tracking

- Google Ads provides free call tracking limited to AdWords traffic. Paid solutions (CallRail, PhoneWagon, Call Tracking Metrics) track calls from all traffic sources, integrate with Google Analytics and offer more complete attribution at a cost [L0234.004].
- The global site tag (Google's universal tracking code) must be installed on your website for call conversion tracking to work. If Google Analytics or other Google conversion tracking is already set up, the tag is present and no new code is needed [L0234.010].
- If you enter your actual website phone number during setup, Google scans your website and replaces all instances with the forwarding number. If you skip this step, you must update the HTML code manually [L0234.012].
- Set up call conversion tracking [L0234.013]:
  1. In Google Ads, navigate to Conversions (search for conversions in the top menu).
  2. Click New Conversion.
  3. Select Track phone calls, then choose Calls on website (not call extensions or call-only ads).
  4. Enter a conversion name such as Lead.
  5. Optionally set a revenue value. Leaving this blank is acceptable.
  6. Choose whether multiple calls from the same person count as 1 conversion or multiple conversions (typically 1 total).
  7. Set the minimum call duration to count as a conversion. 20 seconds is standard.
  8. Confirm the lookback window is set to 30 days.
  9. Confirm the attribution model is set to Last click.
  10. For the conversion tracking tag, confirm or select Global site tag if Google Analytics or other conversions are already set up.
  11. Enter your current website phone number in the phone number field.
  12. Google will automatically find and replace this number with a forwarding number on your website.
  13. Click Next to complete setup.
  14. Verify tracking is working by checking the tracking status and optionally using Google Tag Assistant. [L0234.013]

### Account Separation per Store

- Each store should have its own separate Google accounts and its own email address on all Google properties. This makes it easier to sell one store later, because its data and ad history are not mixed with the others [L0358.010, 2020].
- Use a separate Google Ads account for each business [L0717.008].
- Each business needs its own separate set of Google accounts. Do not send product feeds from multiple businesses into one Merchant Center account, and do not run ads for multiple businesses from one Google Ads account [L0727.011, 2021-22].
- Each unrelated store needs its own Google Ads account. Stores in the same network that can cross-promote to each other's customers, such as a bounce house store, a trampoline store and a swing set store, can share one account [L0837.045, 2025].
- Do not run two separate Google Ads accounts for the same store, because they compete with each other. Splitting the data across accounts also slows the learning of each account [L0962.055, 2021].
- Ads for the same store from two accounts are only less harmful if one account runs video ads and the other runs Shopping ads on non-overlapping products. Even then this setup is not recommended, because both accounts learn slowly [L0962.056, 2021].
- Google and Facebook ad systems learn from data concentrated in a single account. Spreading data across several accounts makes each one learn more slowly [L0962.057, 2021].
- Two stores in the same market selling the same products can compete against each other in Google Ads. If you run two stores in one market, keep their product ranges different [L0905.023, 2021-22].
- Multiple Google Ads accounts under different business entities, with different email addresses and billing information, are allowed. Each account is managed separately, and issues with one do not typically affect the others [L0278.039, 2025].
- For a new business, create a new Google Ads account [L1092.074, 2022].

## Google Merchant Center Setup and Verification

### Merchant Center's role in the setup

- Google Merchant Center connects your Shopify store to Google's ecosystem. It pulls product data from Shopify and makes those products eligible for free Google Product Listings, organic Google Shopping results and paid Google Shopping Ads. [L0181.001]
- Merchant Center is the account that receives product data from the Shopify store and passes it to Google Ads, where Shopping campaigns are built. Its free listings show products in Google surfaces without paid ads, but bring only limited traffic. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.001]
- It is required before Shopping campaigns can run, and the product feed is built there. It stores product data and formats it for Google Shopping ads. (older, 2021-22) [L0726.001]
- It is the interface that passes your store's product data to Google so products can appear in free product listings and Shopping ads. It takes product data from Shopify and is set up separately from the Google & YouTube app. [L0729.002]
- It is the connection between a Shopify store and Google. It pulls product data such as images, descriptions, titles, prices, barcode numbers and manufacturer part numbers into the product feed used for Shopping ads. (older, 2021-22) [L0739.015]
- Google builds the product feed from the connected Shopify store through Merchant Center, pulling images, titles, descriptions, prices, barcodes (GTIN) and manufacturer part numbers. Google matches these data points against searches to decide where ads are eligible. (older, 2021-22) [L0741.007]
- Your product feed is sent to Merchant Center, and from there it is used by Google Ads. [L0762.008]
- All products are entered in Merchant Center, and active listings, shopping announcements, tax and shipping are configured there. Some Merchant Center functions were being moved into the Google Ads interface, so a future setup may run through Google Ads alone. [L0732.001]
- Merchant Center holds the product feed Google uses for Shopping listings. Its tips cover correct product data so that listings are approved and shown. (older, 2020) [L1087.006]

### Accounts, identity and ownership

#### Login and email
- Use the same Google Workspace email address to log in to Merchant Center that you use for Google Analytics and Google Search Console. This makes all Google platforms connect properly. [L0181.003]
- Use the same email address for Google Analytics, Google Ads and Merchant Center. (older, 2019) [L0467.021]
- Sign in with the same Google Workspace email used for Google Analytics and Google Search Console before starting the sign-up. [L0729.001]
- For the business sign-up, use the business email address, for example the store's sales mailbox. (older, 2021-22) [L0726.006]

#### Account structure
- Each store should have its own Google Merchant Center account. Separate accounts keep each store's product feed, approvals and suspension issues independent. [L1114.071]
- Only one website can be linked per Merchant Center account. A second website requires an advanced account. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.016]
- Before clicking Link in Merchant Center, confirm that the Google Ads customer ID shown there is the account meant for Shopping campaigns. Linking the wrong account pulls the Merchant Center product data into it. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.040]

#### Business country and time zone
- The business country cannot be changed after the account is opened. Set it to the country you sell in, which is not necessarily the country where you live. (older, 2021-22) [L0726.004]
- The business country should be the country where the business is headquartered or legally registered and where it sells. It is fixed once the account is opened, so confirm it before submitting. The owner's personal location does not decide this field. (older, 2021-22) [L0726.024]
- The registered country must be the country where the business operates. [L0729.005]
- The Merchant Center time zone is used to calculate and report performance. Choose the time zone of the business, not necessarily your own location. (older, 2021-22) [L0726.005]
- Set the time zone to the business's time zone when creating the account. (older, 2021-22) [L0726.006]

#### Domain verification and claim
- Google requires proof that you own the website before you can sell products through Merchant Center. Website ownership cannot be verified through the default Google Analytics setup. [L0732.002]
- **Sources differ:** L0732.002 says the default Google Analytics setup cannot verify ownership. L0728.012 and L0467.021 (2019) describe verifying through Google Analytics with the same email. Both are stated as given. L0732.003 presents the HTML tag route without tying it to a condition. [L0732.002, L0728.012, L0467.021, L0732.003]

##### Verification methods

| Method | Steps | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google Analytics | Use the same email as the Analytics account and select the existing Analytics account when prompted | L0728.012 | Verifies automatically if Analytics confirms domain ownership |
| Google Analytics (older) | Choose verify through Google Analytics, click Next | L0467.021 (older, 2019) | Analytics code is already on the site and the domain matches |
| HTML tag | Copy the Google verification code from Merchant Center and paste it into theme.liquid | L0732.003 | Paste in the head section |
| Google Tag Manager | Alternative if already installed on the site | L0732.004 | The verification tag must stay in the head section so ownership keeps being recognised |
| Google Workspace domain | Meta tag method first, or DNS records method, which can be updated directly in Shopify | L1094.046 | Check the pasted code for missing characters such as brackets, since that can stop verification |

##### Verify and claim through Google Analytics
1. Enter the website URL in Google Merchant Center. [L0728.012]
2. Use the same email address as the Google Analytics account, and select the existing Google Analytics account when prompted. [L0728.012]
3. Click Verify URL. If Google Analytics confirms domain ownership, the URL is verified automatically. [L0728.012]
4. Click Claim to claim the domain. [L0728.012]

##### Verify and claim through an HTML tag (Source A, undated)
1. Sign up for Google Merchant Center and enter your business name and website URL. [L0732.003]
2. Copy the Google verification code (HTML tag) from Merchant Center. [L0732.003]
3. In Shopify, go to Themes and edit the code of theme.liquid. [L0732.003]
4. Find the head section of the file (search for the head tag) and paste the verification code there. [L0732.003]
5. Save the theme and wait about 5 minutes for the change to be picked up. [L0732.003]
6. Return to Merchant Center and click Verify. [L0732.003]

##### Placing the tag in the editor
- To place the verification tag, open Themes, edit theme.liquid, and use the editor's find function to search for the closing head tag. Paste the verification code just above it, save the file, and then click Verify in Merchant Center. [L0732.023]
- In the example theme, the tag was pasted directly before the closing head tag on line 68. (older, 2019 to 2022 cases are not dated in this unit; the procedure is from Source A) [L0728.014]

##### Workaround for the "malformed" error
- The error "Google Analytics tracking code on your site looks malformed" can appear when verifying through Google Analytics, even when the tracking code is correct. It often happens with custom or test themes. [L0728.013]
- Workaround (HTML tag verification):
  1. In Google Merchant Center, choose the option that you have access to your server and copy the HTML verification tag to the clipboard. [L0728.014]
  2. In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes, open the theme (customize it, for example a copy of the live theme), and click Edit code. [L0728.014]
  3. Open the file theme.liquid. [L0728.014]
  4. Paste the copied HTML tag directly before the closing `</head>` tag. [L0728.014]
  5. Click Save. [L0728.014]
  6. Open the website to check that nothing is broken. [L0728.014]
  7. Return to Google Merchant Center, click Verify URL, then click Claim. [L0728.014]
- Test the storefront after adding a verification tag to theme.liquid to confirm the page still loads without broken code, before returning to Google Merchant Center. [L0728.015]

##### Claim and checks
- Verify and claim the website in Merchant Center: (older, 2021-22) [L0731.017]
  1. Enter the website URL and click Continue. [L0731.017]
  2. Wait until Merchant Center shows the site as verified, which confirms the site is live. [L0731.017]
  3. Click Claim website. Claiming stops other accounts from using the same URL. [L0731.017]
- Enter the website URL with its full address beginning with https:// or http://. [L0731.016]
- Check in Merchant Center that the website is verified and claimed before finishing business information. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.007]
- Check that the website is claimed and verified in Business information before moving on to branding or other settings. (older, 2021-22) [L0727.027]
- If Merchant Center asks to verify a site that was verified before, the usual cause is that another Google login or person verified the store name, or someone edited the site and removed the verification code. Check who has access to the site first. (older, 2019) [L0467.020]

### Choosing the Shopify connection path

- When Google detects your Shopify store, do not click **Connect to Shopify** and do not use the Google & YouTube app for product submission. Click **Continue to Merchant Center** instead. [L0181.004]
- When Merchant Center offers to connect to Shopify, decline it and choose **Continue to Merchant Center**. The Shopify connection uses the Google & YouTube app, which is not the method used to submit products. [L0729.004]
- Do not follow the Shopify-guided option during Merchant Center sign-up. Skip it and connect Shopify to Merchant Center afterwards. (older, 2021-22) [L0726.007]
- Skip the Shopify option at sign-up and connect Shopify later. (older, 2021-22) [L0726.006]

### Sign-up procedures

Four procedures from the sources are kept complete. They differ in length and detail. Use the one that fits the account type and tooling of the store.

#### Sign-up sequence A (Source A, 11 steps)
1. Open the Google Merchant Center signup page and click **Start now**. [L0181.008]
2. Answer the initial questions: select **Yes** for selling products online, enter your store website URL, select **No** for having a physical store, then click **Continue**. [L0181.008]
3. When Google detects your Shopify store, do NOT click **Connect to Shopify** and do NOT use the Google & YouTube app for product submission; click **Continue to Merchant Center** instead. [L0181.008]
4. Confirm your business name (it should match your store name) and select your registered business country, then click **Continue to Merchant Center**. [L0181.008]
5. Enter your registered business address (home address if sole proprietor, business address if you have one). This address is not shown to customers. Click **Continue**. [L0181.008]
6. Verify your domain, which should already be verified via Search Console; confirm ownership verification and click **Continue**. [L0181.008]
7. Select only the countries where you actually sell (example: United States). Click **Continue**. [L0181.008]
8. Select **Enter delivery times manually**. Choose your store's order cutoff time. Enter your handling time and transit time to match your shipping policy, ensuring totals match what is stated on your site. Select **Free shipping** if applicable. Click **Save**. [L0181.008]
9. Paste the URL of your Returns & Refunds policy. Select the countries you accept returns from. Confirm acceptance of both defective and non-defective products. Enter your return window to match your policy (example: 30 days). Select **mail** as the return method. Specify return shipping responsibility to match your policy. Select **No cost** for restocking fee if applicable. Enter refund processing time to match your policy. Review and click **Save**. [L0181.008]
10. Skip linking Google Ads for now; it will be set up later after your products are approved. [L0181.008]
11. Go to Settings > Data Sources, locate **Found by Google**, and click **Hide all automatically found products**. [L0181.008]

#### Sign-up sequence B (Source A, 19 steps)
1. Sign in with the same Google Workspace email used for Google Analytics and Google Search Console. [L0729.001]
2. Open the Merchant Center sign-up page and click **Start now**. [L0729.001]
3. Answer **Do you sell products online?** with Yes and enter the store's website URL. [L0729.001]
4. Answer **Do you have a physical store?** with No, then click **Continue**. [L0729.001]
5. Confirm that the store's compliance fixes are finished before continuing. [L0729.001]
6. When offered two connection options, do not click **Connect to Shopify**. Click **Continue to Merchant Center**. [L0729.001]
7. Confirm that you sell products (not services) and continue. [L0729.001]
8. Keep the business name equal to the store name, and set the registered country to the country where you do business. Click **Continue**. [L0729.001]
9. Enter the registered business address and continue. [L0729.001]
10. Accept the automatic domain verification, which Search Console already completed, and continue. [L0729.001]
11. Select only the countries where you sell, for example the United States. [L0729.001]
12. For shipping, set order cutoff time, handling time and transit time manually and match them to the shipping policy page. Enter the handling and transit times, then continue. [L0729.001]
13. Choose free shipping for all customers with no conditional values, then click **Save**. [L0729.001]
14. Paste the return policy URL, select whether returns are accepted for defective and non-defective products, and state whether exchanges are accepted, all exactly as the website's return policy says. [L0729.001]
15. Enter the return window, return method, who pays return shipping, restocking fee and refund processing time, matching the policies, then click **Next**. [L0729.001]
16. Review the summary, confirm it is accurate, and click **Save**. [L0729.001]
17. Skip linking Google Ads for now. [L0729.001]
18. Open **View products**. Products show "processing" first and lose that label once approved. [L0729.001]
19. Go to Settings > Data sources, open **Actions** and choose **Hide all automatically found products** so that the "Provided by you" source is used. [L0729.001]

#### Account creation for Shopping ads (Source A, 11 steps)
1. Open the Google Merchant Center page and click **Get started**, then **Get started** again. [L0728.002]
2. Enter the country, the business display name (for example the store name), and the time zone, then click **Continue**. [L0728.002]
3. Accept the terms of service and choose whether to receive updates, then click **Continue**. [L0728.002]
4. Select the programs that fit your goals. Select Shopping actions only if you want it, knowing it needs more business history and product understanding, then click **Continue**. [L0728.002]
5. Confirm your choices and create the account. [L0728.002]
6. In the setup guides, start with the shopping ads setup (listed first, most important). [L0728.002]
7. Configure tax (see tax section), then shipping (see shipping section). [L0728.002]
8. Add the store website URL, verify it and claim the domain (see verification section). [L0728.002]
9. Upload the logo and set branding (accent color, square and rectangular logo). [L0728.002]
10. Link the Google Ads account to Google Merchant Center and approve the link request in Google Ads. [L0728.002]
11. Upload the product feed (covered in the next step of the course; this lesson does not include it). [L0728.002]

#### Account creation for Google Shopping (Source B, 9 steps; older, 2021-22)
1. Open the Google Merchant Center sign-up page using the business email address, for example the store's sales mailbox. [L0726.006]
2. Click **Get started**. [L0726.006]
3. Enter the business name. Customers see it in product listings, and it becomes the Merchant Center account name. [L0726.006]
4. Select the business country, which is the country where you sell. [L0726.006]
5. Select the time zone of the business. [L0726.006]
6. Skip the Shopify option at this stage and connect Shopify later. [L0726.006]
7. Decide whether to receive marketing emails. This is optional. [L0726.006]
8. Accept the Merchant Center terms of service and create the account. [L0726.006]
9. Leave the remaining setup questions open. They are completed when the product feed is built. [L0726.006]

### Business information

#### Where to find it
- In Merchant Center, open the cogwheel (Settings) at the top right and go to Business information. Complete all of its fields, verify the domain and phone number, and add your branding. Incomplete business information can get the account suspended. [L1145.041]
- Business information is under the Tools section of the left menu, next to Shipping and returns, Regions and Sales tax. (older, 2021-22) [L0727.026]
- The left menu holds these groups (older, 2021-22) [L0730.019]:
  - Overview
  - Products: All products, Feeds, Diagnostics
  - Performance
  - Marketing
  - Growth
  - Tools: Shipping and returns, Regions, Sales tax, Shopping ads setup, Free listings setup, Comparison Shopping Services
  - Settings: Account settings, Account access, Preferences, Linked accounts, Automatic improvements, SFTP / FTP / GCS, Content API
  - Business information is one of the settings pages and holds the About your business and Branding tabs.
- If the interface is missing a menu such as Manage programs or Growth, the account may be in a Google test. Contact Merchant Center support, state the missing menu, and ask to be removed from the test or shown where to find it. (2023) [L0970.119]

#### Fields in About your business
- The About your business page contains: Business display name, Business address (Address line 1, Address line 2, City, State/Province, Postal/ZIP code, Country), Phone number, Website, and Customer service contact (URL, E-mail, Phone). (older, 2021-22) [L0730.020, L0727.026]
- Click Save after entering the address. Complete the phone verification and customer service contact in the same tab. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.020]
- The page for Shopping ads customer service contact fields is: Website, E-mail and Phone. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.006]

#### Business display name
- Keep the business name equal to the store name, and do not change it. [L0729.005]
- Changing the business display name requires re-submitting product data before the new name takes effect. (older, 2021-22) [L0727.027, L0730.021]

#### Business address
- The registered business address must match where the business is actually set up. A sole proprietor uses their home address, while an LLC may enter a business address. The address is not shown to customers. [L0729.006]
- **Sources differ:** L0729.006 and L0181.008 accept a home address for a sole proprietor. A 2020 unit reports that a residential home address on a Merchant Center account or website may cause problems, with one reported case asking for photos of a warehouse.
