5. Repeat the review regularly, because new search terms appear over time. [L0510.018]

Procedure for adding converting terms (quarterly cadence):

1. Pull the search term report and find search terms that already convert. [L0454.028]
2. Add those converting terms to the beginning of the relevant product titles to earn more impressions. [L0454.028]
3. Repeat this review about once a quarter, around four times a year. [L0454.028]
4. Optionally, use a feed optimiser that supports A/B testing to test title changes before rolling them out. [L0454.028]

Examples of impressions gained by adding converting generic or brand terms to the front of a title. Use only terms that already appear with conversions in the search term report:

- Adding bridal shoes to a sandal title. [L0454.052]
- Adding tuxedo to a tuxedo title. [L0454.052]
- Adding a brand name such as Adidas slides to a sandal title. [L0454.052]

#### Keyword placement by attribute

- Only put a model or manufacturer part number into a title if customers search for it. Check the search term report for that number. If it appears there, include it. If not, it does not need to be there. [L1456.013]
- Put SKU and barcode information in the product description, since buyers search for these identifiers and they help the product rank for those terms. (older advice, 2022) [L1281.110]
- Keep the product's keyword focus to the brand name, the supplier's name and product identifiers (product name, SKU, MPN or other supplier identifier). Do not chase extra keywords on the product page. (2023) [L0964.060]
- Titles that include a SKU are a supplier-by-supplier decision. Check how the top competitors title the same products in search and follow their pattern. [L1283.041]
- Google Merchant Center is not supposed to flag SKU numbers in SEO titles. If titles are flagged, check the content against the flagged issue instead of removing SKUs by default. [L0805.049]
- Use exact supplier product names and SKUs in listings, because organic search rankings accelerate when you sell specific brands and use those names. [L0163.004]

#### Titles for variants and bundles

- Google matches Shopping products to search terms mainly through the title, so a variant with a different product title is a different feed item. For bundles, keep the same core product title and add a short suffix such as `Gold Bundle` to differentiate them (older advice, 2021-22). [L1456.010]
- Whether to use separate product pages for each variant, or one page with variants, is decided by checking how the top competitors in the niche structure their products. [L1283.042]

### Title Research and Competitor Checks

- Competitor check procedure (older advice, 2020):
  1. Search incognito on Google for the keywords your ad appears for. [L0551.046]
  2. Compare your listing to the competitors that appear. [L0551.046]
  3. Improve your listing title and details to match or beat the better listings. [L0551.046]
  4. Check the click-through rate again after the changes. [L0551.046]
- Shopping competitor exploitation procedure:
  1. Open Google Ads Shopping campaign. [L0208.006]
  2. Check which products receive the most impressions and where clicks land. [L0208.006]
  3. Visit your store's pages for those top-performing products. [L0208.006]
  4. Compare each page to competitors' product pages for identical or similar items. [L0208.006]
  5. Identify specific improvements you can make to win that traffic away from competitors (Module 5.10: Exploit their weakness). [L0208.006]
- Generic keywords on product pages can still trigger impressions, even though brand-name searches will be fewer. Google Shopping ads match searches to the keywords on each product page in the feed (older advice, 2020). [L1088.040]
- Keyword discovery procedure for titles:
  1. Use AI to generate multiple product title variants for the same product, each highlighting a different keyword or customer angle (dietary benefits, ingredients, meal context, product type). [L0220.029]
  2. Extract the primary keywords or benefit angles from each variant (for example `keto-friendly`, `low-calorie`, `gluten-free`). [L0220.029]
  3. Enter each extracted keyword into Google Ads Keyword Planner, adding product-type suffixes (for example `keto-friendly sauce`, `low-calorie dip`, `gluten-free dressing`). [L0220.029]
  4. Compare monthly search volumes to identify which keywords or angles have the strongest buyer demand. [L0220.029]
  5. Deploy the title variants that correspond to the highest-search-volume keywords to your Google Shopping feed. [L0220.029]
- Use negative keywords where a title names another product. Example: a front bumper titled with a Dodge Ram model may appear for people searching for the vehicle itself, which causes low CTR in the automotive space. (older advice, 2021-22) [L0879.029]

### Product Title Duplication and Portfolio Strategy

- Shopping results reward a portfolio of well-titled products over a single optimised listing. Several products from the same seller can appear in one results row, so build strong titles across the whole catalogue rather than perfecting one ad. [L0220.013]
- Feed duplication means creating multiple titles for the same product that target different keywords, use cases and customer angles. This vastly expands audience and keyword coverage, because one product can appear several times with titles optimised for different search intents. [L0220.021]

### Branded vs Unbranded Titles

Sources differ on whether brand or keyword comes first. Use the rule that applies to your product type:

| Product type | Title order | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generic or unbranded, keyword-led | Keyword first, then brand, product name, descriptors | [L0510.017, L1031.023] | Current (Source A, undated; 2023 formula) |
| Branded product with a searched brand and model | Brand, model number, product type, one or two key dimensions | [L1170.050] | Older (2021-22) |
| High-ticket with a manufacturer name customers already search | Manufacturer's product name, usually the converting title | [L1170.011] | Older (2021-22) |

Details for each row:

- **Generic or unbranded:** keyword first. The brand follows, then product name and descriptors. [L0510.017, L1031.023]
- **Branded products:** the pattern is brand name, then model number, then product type, then one or two key dimensions. Customers search for the brand and model string first, so placing it at the start keeps the most-searched terms in the strongest positions. Examples in the same pattern: `Northwind Aurora 900 Pool Heat Pump 15kW` and `Harbor Lux HL-40 Walk-In Bath Tub 60 x 32 in`. (older advice, 2021-22) [L1170.050]
- **Manufacturer name:** for high-ticket dropshipping, the manufacturer's product name is usually the title that converts best, in roughly nine out of ten cases, because customers already search for it. Exceptions exist but are rare. (older advice, 2021-22) [L1170.011]
- **Brand inclusion:** including the brand name in the title is typically fine and often useful when brands sell items that go together. Add it unless there is a specific reason not to. [L0803.046]
- **Branded titles with a unique brand:** if the Google Shopping price is higher than competitors', the first image and title must signal a more premium brand. Combine a unique brand name with the main product keyword, and collect reviews, since they help justify the higher price in results. [L0788.060]
- **Branded or unbranded, first image and title:** the first image is the main differentiator because shoppers see it first. Use a branded product name that also contains the main product keyword. [L0788.016]

Unbranded and invented names:

- A self-invented product name has no search demand. Customers will not find it unless you pay for separate awareness campaigns, which is costly and rarely worth it. (older advice, 2021-22) [L1170.012]
- Do not invent product names for high-ticket listings. Listings with invented names received noticeably fewer impressions than listings using the supplier or manufacturer name. (older advice, 2021-22) [L1170.015]
- The most converting search terms are the most specific to the individual product, whether or not it has a brand. Titles should describe the product accurately so they match what customers type. (older advice, 2021-22) [L1170.014]
- Rewrite supplier titles that do not match what customers type, and fix poor titles before launch, since they can be refined later (older advice, 2021-22). [L1145.036]

Procedure for unbranded product titles (older advice, 2021-22):

1. Research the terms customers use to describe the product type. [L1170.013]
2. List the product's features, such as size, colour, material, shape and model. [L1170.013]
3. Combine three or four of the most searched features into the title and end it with the product noun. [L1170.013]

Example of a title that fails and a title that works (older advice, 2021-22):

- A title that only says `surfboard` rarely converts on Google Shopping because it is top of funnel. [L1170.017]
- A title that combines size, colour, material and shape with the noun matches the searches buyers actually enter. [L1170.017]

Product type and attributes in titles:

- In Google Shopping, the title is a main signal for which searches a product can match. A title naming the product type plus key attributes (capacity, zones, size) makes the product eligible for more relevant searches. You control this through feed data, not by choosing search terms directly. (older advice, 2021-22) [L0739.030]
- In Google Shopping you cannot choose keywords directly as you would in Search. Add the relevant keywords into product titles and store content so the product appears for those searches. [L0788.020]
- For a flip-flop product, keep the core product type and the most important attributes in the title. Put gender, brand, colour, style words and synonyms such as casual sandal, slip-on or thong sandal in the description. This lets one product match many related searches without making the title too long. [L1328.040]

### Product Descriptions

- Google Merchant Center may reject products that have no description, so do not paste only the title. Generate a real description as soon as possible. [L0471.046]
- Put the description first and the features under it, because Google Merchant Center reads the start of the description first. (2023) [L0964.061]
- Google weighs roughly the first 300 words of the description most heavily, so put the key matching terms there. Longer text beyond that matters less for matching. (older advice, 2021-22) [L1170.006]
- Put SKU and barcode information in the description, since buyers search for these identifiers. (older advice, 2022) [L1281.110]
- Keep the description focus on brand, supplier name and identifiers. Synonym and variant terms (such as casual sandal, slip-on or thong sandal) belong in the description, not the title. The 2023 rule and the flip-flop example apply to different terms, so use both. [L0964.060, L1328.040]
- If product page data differs from the feed, the mismatch can read as a poor landing page experience. Most high-ticket dropshippers keep page data close to the feed, so this is less likely to be a problem for them (older advice, 2021-22). [L0879.015]
- Complete feed data feeds into Quality Score: title, description, Google product category, MPN and GTIN where they exist, gender, age group, condition and image quality. Gaps or weak data lower the audience quality the ad can reach (older advice, 2021-22). [L0879.013]

### Images: Background and Policy

#### Background

Sources disagree on the background requirement. Both values and their use cases:

| Source | Requirement | When it applies |
|---|---|---|
| Source A, 2025 | Main photo must be white. Get at least one white-background image per product from the supplier before launching. | Use as the default for all Shopping products. [L0972.096] |
| Source A, 2023 | Blue background can run without issues, but white or transparent is preferred by feed providers. | Use only where a blue background is already approved and no white version exists. [L1094.039] |
| Source B, 2021-22 (older) | Flat-background images must use plain white, not black, green or patterned. Lifestyle photos may use other backgrounds. | Apply to flat product shots. Lifestyle images are a separate category. [L1163.010] |

- Google Shopping and remarketing campaigns use white-background product images. [L1115.050]
- Google's written image policy may lag behind what is actually accepted for Shopping. Check the current policy before assuming a style is forbidden. Competitor ads with alternative image styles are a signal of what passes review. [L0882.004]
- Plain white is the safe default, but on a results page full of similar white backgrounds, it is hard to stand out. Lifestyle or in-context images showing the product in use can create differentiation. [L0882.003]
- Keep the supplier's stock image as the main image unchanged, because Shopping needs a white-background main image. Only supplementary images on the product page can be customised, for example in Canva, to make a private-label product look unique. [L1015.015]

Procedure for changing a background to white in Canva:

1. Upload the product image with the blue background to Canva. [L1094.040]
2. Use the background eraser tool to remove the background. [L1094.040]
3. Set the background to white and save the image. [L1094.040]

#### Text, logos and overlays

Sources agree that the main image must contain no text, logos or overlays. Apply the following:

| Element | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Text on image | Merchant Center rejects product images that have text. Use a clean photo as the feed image. | [L0803.045] |
| Text, badges, overlays | Do not put text or overlays, such as free shipping badges, on product images in Merchant Center. This can get products disabled. Free shipping can still show in the ad as a setting. (2023) | [L1094.041] |
| Own text or logos | Product images may not contain text except branding that is part of the product itself. Do not add your own logos, slogans or words to the background. (older advice, 2021-22) | [L1163.011] |
| Supplier logos | Remove supplier logos or graphics from the primary image, because Shopping does not allow such graphics. (2023) | [L0470.036] |
| Borders and overlays | The Merchant Center main image must not contain any extra element. A border or overlay counts as an error and blocks approval. (2024) | [L0971.063] |

- Replace images for social platforms with unique themed images, because Shopping and remarketing use white-background product images but social performs better with themed visuals (2024). [L1115.050]

#### Image delivery and troubleshooting

- Running Shopping campaigns displays the product image next to the ad by default. Merchant Center submission and Shopping campaign setup are required (2021). [L0247.047]
- Shoppers see the image before the click. The photo and visible product carry much of the decision to click. A product that looks like every other listing gets fewer clicks. [L1508.003]
- Image determines whether a shopper clicks, while title determines whether the product appears. [L0220.026]
- Google Shopping ads use product images from your product pages, so no separate ad creatives are needed in the standard setup. [L0972.064]
- Shopping ads depend on custom content, such as professional photos and edited videos. Generic supplier footage is not enough for dropshipping. [L0577.048]
- If a feed image is not shown next to listings even though Merchant Center approved it, check the image URL. Click the image links to confirm they open, since a broken link prevents the image from showing. (2023) [L0470.072]

Procedure for moving an approved AI image into a Shopping listing:

1. Generate and select the image that meets the front-facing, spacing and no-text requirements. [L0882.017]
2. Download the image file. [L0882.017]
3. Upload it to the matching product listing in Google Merchant Center. [L0882.017, L0882.018]
4. If the product already converts, duplicate the listing and run the new image as a split test instead of replacing the original. [L0882.017]

Merchant Center is where product images are uploaded to individual Shopping listings, and where a duplicated listing is created for a split test. [L0882.018]

### Image and Title A/B Tests

Procedure for a clean image split test:

1. Do not simply replace the image of a listing that already converts well. [L0882.005]
2. Duplicate the product listing in the product feed. [L0882.005]
3. Swap only the image on the copy. Keep the same title, price and product data. [L0882.005]
4. Run both listings inside the same Shopping campaign with the same bid, the same budget and the same audience. [L0882.005]
5. Wait until both have enough impressions for the click-through rate to be meaningful. [L0882.005]
6. Keep the listing with the higher CTR as the winner and delete the loser. [L0882.005]

- The image must be the only variable in a Shopping image test. Otherwise the CTR difference cannot be attributed to it. Same price, bid, budget and audience keep both listings competing under identical conditions. [L0882.006]
- Title tests can be run through a feed optimiser that supports A/B testing before title changes are rolled out. [L0454.028]

### Star Ratings and Reviews

- Rich snippets star review apps from the Shopify App Store show star ratings in Google Shopping ads. Prices vary widely, so compare several before choosing one (2020). [L0852.067]
- Collect reviews, since Google displays them in Shopping ads. [L0788.016]
- Reviews help justify a higher price in results, especially where the price is above competitors'. [L0788.060]
- Google Merchant Center's Review feeds section can be uploaded directly or through an app, and should be reviewed regularly. [L0732.020]
- Star ratings are among the elements that affect whether a Shopping ad gets clicked, alongside title, image, price and brand. [L1031.022]
- In a study of thousands of Shopping ads, the title was the most influential element for CTR, ahead of images, star ratings and price. [L0510.019]

### Merchant Center Promotions

#### Setup

Procedure for creating promotions (2023):

1. Create the promotion in Google Merchant Center or in Shopify's Google channel settings, following the Shopify support guide for promotions in Google Shopping ads. [L0430.005]
2. Set the promotion's discount code, date range and eligible products. [L0430.005]
3. Confirm the promotion is approved in Merchant Center before relying on it in ads. [L0430.005]

Example procedure with coupon codes (2025):

1. Create the promotion in Merchant Center, for example 10% off with coupon code FF. [L0255.043]
2. Ensure the coupon code is active on the website for the entire promotion period. [L0255.043]
3. Double and triple check that the code works throughout the duration. [L0255.043]
4. If the code expires or stops working before the promotion end date, Google may suspend the Merchant Center account. [L0255.043]

Setup facts:

- Promotions are added in Merchant Center as an add-on to the Shopping account. (2025) [L0472.014, L0472.073]
- Promotions are created in Merchant Center. A Google support document explains how to set one up for Shopping ads, and promotions attach discount or offer messaging to products shown in Shopping results. [L1093.001]
- Google Shopping ads are supported by the Merchant Center promotions setting. (2022) [L0665.082]
- Create coupon-code promotions in Merchant Center to show the discount on Google Shopping listings. [L0667.007]
- Promotions are created inside Merchant Center to show discount offers in Google Shopping results. Set them up before expecting them to appear on listings. (2025) [L0675.008]
- Merchant Center sections to review regularly are Promotions (shown next to product titles in Shopping ads) and Review feeds (uploaded directly or through an app). [L0732.020]

#### What promotions can show

- Google Shopping promotions can show badges such as low price or great pick alongside ads quickly, without needing store history. They are the fastest way to match competitors' badges (2022). [L0429.064]
- Promotions can add extra clickable text next to the store name in results, which can improve CTR (2021). [L0469.097]
- Shopping ads can show promotional text such as a price advantage over another retailer. In the example shown, a 31% price drop was displayed in the ad. [L0762.007]
- Promotions display discount labels such as `save 350, expires in 4 days`. [L0472.013]
- Advertise active discounts through the promotion function in Merchant Center. The discounts then appear in Shopping ads, which gives a visual advantage over competitors. [L1357.009]
- Use Merchant Center promotions so your offer appears in Google Shopping results. This gives an advantage over stores that do not run promotions there. [L0920.009]

#### Where promotions are not shown

- Google Shopping promotions are not shown in the free organic section. Low-margin products can therefore stay in the free listings, while promotions are set up only for the best-selling, highest-margin products in the new best-seller campaigns. (2025) [L0472.013]

#### Eligibility and rules

- Promotions accept only percent-off or fixed-amount offers. A bundle is treated as a new product that must be submitted to Merchant Center, not as a promotion on an existing product (2020). [L1088.041]
- Google's shipping promotion policy changed, so a free shipping promotion may be rejected for requiring a coupon code. Check the Merchant Center promotion policy before running it (2024). [L1115.052]
- Do not create a free shipping promotion with a coupon code just to satisfy the policy, because this can interfere with other coupons. Use another structure, such as a small fixed discount on a large order (2024). [L1115.047]
- Free shipping can be shown as a setting or tag in Merchant Center, and these special tags can appear in Google Shopping ads. [L0788.017, L1094.041]

#### Case

- A store with little sales despite on-site optimisations added Google Shopping promotions to its shopping ads. Sales went from near zero to roughly 20 to 25 within a couple of weeks (2025). [L0472.073]

### Feed Effects on Quality Score, CTR and Impressions

#### Quality Score

- Complete feed data feeds into Quality Score (older advice, 2021-22). [L0879.013]
- Platform gains stack in a positive feedback loop. A better title raises CTR. Higher CTR raises quality score, which lowers CPC and improves position. Each optimisation makes the next one more valuable. [L0510.024]
- Case: an advertiser selling a golf-ball type product optimised its campaign for CTR. CTR rose by 108%, cost per click fell by 25%, and quality score rose by 60%. The change let the advertiser get cheaper clicks than competitors who were paying more for weaker ads. [L0510.016]

#### CTR

- CTR can be improved through product titles, descriptions, images, bids and negatives. After the click, the store experience should keep visitors engaged (2022). [L0969.084]
- A title that is optimised to raise CTR while keeping the product accurate reduces wasted clicks. [L0510.016, L0969.084]
- To raise CTR without changing targeting, spell out in the ad why a premium product is worth its price, such as what makes it more premium than cheaper alternatives. Clear reasons for a higher price attract the right clicks. [L0327.027]
- Intentionally decreasing CTR can improve profitability. Example: if your product costs $900 and competitors charge $800, include the price in ads to reduce clicks from price-focused customers. This lowers CTR but saves money and increases ROAS. [L0327.007]

#### Impressions

- Moving a commonly searched term to the front of the title raised CTR for those terms by about 88%, and lifted impressions across all products by about 18%. This comes from a study of thousands of Shopping ads. [L0510.019]
- Title tests in another study reported about a 33% increase in impressions and about a 320% change in revenue. One example reported a 400% increase in impressions after a single word was added to the front of an old title. [L0510.020]
- Adding a converting high-volume generic term to the front of a title increased impressions in the examples shown. [L0454.052]
- Titles improved to rank higher and earn more clicks in organic search also flow into the Shopping feed, so one title edit can help both channels. [L0762.016]

#### Title as an impression lever

- Title is the lever that controls search reach. Image controls click. Keep both in mind when running tests. [L0220.026, L1508.003]

### Competitive Positioning

- A product that looks like every other listing gets fewer clicks, so visible differences in photo and title matter. [L1508.003]
- Ads that are cheaper per click than competitors' often come from a stronger ad, not a lower bid. The golf-ball case shows a CTR-led change that made clicks cheaper than rivals paying more. [L0510.016]

### Review Cadence

- Review converting search terms about once a quarter, around four times a year, and add them to titles. [L0454.028]
- Repeat title review regularly, because new search terms appear over time. [L0510.018]
- Review the feed regularly, not only at launch. [L1170.003]

## Merchant Center Diagnostics, Disapprovals and Free Listings

### Daily Diagnostics Routine

1. Open the Merchant Center home page and check how many products are disapproved [L0732.015].
2. Open Diagnostics to see the exact error for each disapproved product [L0732.015].
3. Fix the errors in the store or feed app, then let the feed update [L0732.015].
4. Check the last upload date in the Feeds section to confirm the feed is refreshing [L0732.015, L0732.025].
5. Confirm that the feed is live and free of errors and warnings, and fix problems immediately. Google's error emails are unreliable, so do not depend on them alone. A feed that is offline for a day or two loses those searches [L0575.005].
6. Spot-check your top 10 to 20 best-selling products:
   1. Confirm they appear in Google Ads and Bing Ads if you run them [L1357.013].
   2. Confirm they show as organic results if you do SEO [L1357.013].
   3. If a product is missing, find the cause and fix it immediately, because customers cannot buy what they cannot find [L1357.013].
7. Check the Overview page. The top right shows free listings with the number of active and disapproved products. Click Diagnostics for the reasons [L0470.057].
8. Do not let disapprovals build up. In an aged store example, 474 products were approved and 81 needed optimization, which means roughly 15% of products were not showing in Shopping. Each unapproved product is a potential loss of sales, so these errors should be fixed quickly [L0732.017].
9. Merchant Center disapproves products that break Google's policies automatically and lists them, so you can see what Google rejects. If the reason for a disapproval is unclear, Google support can explain it [L0732.024].

### Where to Find Diagnostics

- Merchant Center > Products > Diagnostics shows item issues and feed issues for all products, with affected destinations (Shopping ads, Dynamic Remarketing, Free listings), countries and the share of affected past clicks [L0727.018].
- The Diagnostics page has three tabs: Item issues (problems per product), Feed issues, and Account issues (account-wide problems such as suspensions by country) [L0730.009, L0730.023].
- The Products overview graph shows counts of Active, Expiring, Pending and Disapproved items over time [L0730.023].
- Each row in Item issues shows the number of affected items plus two shares: % affected and % affected past clicks. The default date range is the last 30 days up to today. In the example, each issue affected less than 1% of items [L0730.024].
- To filter, set destination to Shopping ads, countries to All and primary feed to All [L0730.009].
- In the Products section, items not approved for Shopping ads are marked [L0732.025].
- The product detail page (Products > All products, then click the product) shows:
  - Item status with the issue [L0730.025].
  - Affected destinations: Shopping ads, Dynamic Remarketing, Free listings [L0730.025].
  - Technical details: Expires in (for example 11 day(s)), Created on, Primary feed, and whether the data comes from the Content API [L0730.025].
- After Google has checked your feed, open Products > Diagnostics and fix every product warning, such as missing barcodes or products without a price [L1145.043].
- The Merchant Center account does not show whether Google Ads is active. Check the Google Ads account for that. Merchant Center shows the feed, approved products, rejected products and errors [L0964.057].
- Merchant Center shows the status of every product feed item. Products flagged with red errors need fixing before they can show, so check that all products are green [L1112.017, older 2021].
- Products > Diagnostics for the specific issue is the first step when fixing a feed error [L0971.064, L1015.001].

### Reading Warnings Versus Violations

- Yellow warning signs are optimization suggestions for ad performance. They are not violations, do not cause a suspension, do not stop ads from running, and are optional to fix [L0727.018, L0730.016, older 2021-22].
- Red disapprovals are the items that must be fixed [L0730.016, older 2021-22].
- Google Merchant Center can show limited reach for policy violations while ads still run. Read the exact warning wording before deciding whether the problem is urgent [L0855.015].
- The restricted reach from a policy violation is fixed by changing the flagged content, not by stopping the campaign [L0855.020].
- Limited performance due to missing value (gtin) means the product still runs but with reduced performance because the barcode is missing [L0727.030].
- A product disapproval or missing GTIN can stop its feed from showing in ad previews. Check the Merchant Center issue report for the affected products and fix them [L0966.084].
- The same Shopping ads policy warning can appear twice in Merchant Center. Treat it as one issue when fixing the feed [L1170.047, older 2021-22].
- Variant-based issues are often not a major problem if the primary products of the store are already approved and showing. It is usually not worth rewriting every variant of every product only for Shopping Actions [L0738.032, older 2021-22].
- A Merchant Center notice that point-of-sale or inventory data for local product listings has expired can usually be ignored when the store's products are already approved and selling. Confirm the product listings and account status before acting on it [L0666.061].
- Without a visible message in Merchant Center, low organic Shopping impressions are not caused by a restriction. A niche-wide restriction would affect every store in that niche, not just one [L0837.002].
- Merchant Center approval problems can delay a new store by about 20 days, so resolve the flagged issues before expecting Shopping traffic [L0667.002].

### Item Issues and Common Fixes

#### Common Item Issues

Diagnostics > Item issues, with the affected field and the meaning for the store (older, Source B 2021-22):

| Issue | Affected field | Meaning and fix |
|---|---|---|
| Violation of Shopping ads policy | Product | Product is blocked by Google's Shopping ads policy; check the item status and either fix the product or request a review if it is wrongly flagged |
| Invalid value (gtin) | GTIN | Barcode is not valid; correct the barcode in Shopify and the supplier data so it flows into the feed |
| Missing value (shipping) | Shipping | Shipping value is missing in the feed; add the shipping setting so it reaches Merchant Center |
| Limited performance due to missing value (gtin) | GTIN | Product still runs but with reduced performance because the barcode is missing; add the GTIN |
| Promotional overlay on image (image link) | Image | Product image contains a promotional overlay; use an image without promotional overlays |
| Low image quality (image link) | Image | Product image is rated low quality; replace it with a sharper, clearer image |
| Value truncated (too long) (title) | Title | Product title is cut off because it exceeds the length limit; shorten the title |
| Excessive capitalization (title) | Title | Title uses too many capital letters; rewrite it in normal capitalization |

[L0727.030]

Common Merchant Center disapproval reasons for a Shopping ads destination, seen in diagnostics (older, Source B 2021-22):
- Violation of Shopping ads policy [L0730.012]
- Invalid value [gtin] [L0730.012]
- Missing value [shipping] [L0730.012]
- Promotional overlay on image [image link] [L0730.012]
- Limited performance due to missing value [gtin] [L0730.012]
- Value truncated (too long) [title] [L0730.012]
- Low image quality [image link] [L0730.012]
- Excessive capitalization [title] [L0730.012]
- Invalid value [gtin] (duplicate or non-valid) [L0730.012]
- Missing or outdated availability updates [availability] [L0730.012]
- Disallowed code in description [description] [L0730.012]

Common Shopping Actions feed issues (older, Source B 2021-22). Each warning shows the affected items and percentage in the Diagnostics view:
- Duplicate GTIN values [L0738.031]
- Potentially inaccurate price [L0738.031]
- Promotional overlay on the image link [L0738.031]
- Same value for differing variants [L0738.031]
- Invalid GTIN or colour [L0738.031]
- Incorrect identifier [L0738.031]
- Ungrouped variants with a matching image link [L0738.031]
- Ambiguous GTIN [L0738.031]
- Character encoding problems in the description (UTF-8) [L0738.031]

Duplicate variant warnings often come from variants that share the same GTIN or other identifiers. Fix them by submitting unique values for each variant, because Google ignores very similar variants and serves a single ad for them (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0738.030].

Product-level disapprovals affect only those products and do not suspend the whole account when they are a small share of the feed (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0730.011].

#### GTIN

- Products showing missing GTIN, MPN or brand errors point to broken product URLs, outdated feed data, or missing brand fields. Verify:
  1. The URLs are working [L0276.055].
  2. The feed updates every 24 hours [L0276.055].
  3. The brand field is populated in your Shopify store [L0276.055].
  4. The brand is mapped correctly in your feed [L0276.055].
- Fix a missing GTIN:
  1. Email the supplier and ask whether each affected product has a GTIN and what it is [L0807.020].
  2. Add the GTIN for every product where the supplier provides one [L0807.020].
  3. Only if no GTIN exists, use the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead, following Google's documentation on when this is allowed [L0807.020].
- Fix a valid disapproval such as an invalid GTIN (older, Source B 2021-22):
  1. Identify the product from the diagnostics list [L0730.015].
  2. In Shopify, open the product and check the barcode value linked to it [L0730.015].
  3. Compare it with the supplier's product information and make sure the values match [L0730.015].
  4. Change the value in Shopify if needed [L0730.015].
  5. The change passes through the feed to Merchant Center and the disapproval updates automatically [L0730.015].
- Errors in product data such as invalid GTIN values should be fixed in the source data (Shopify and supplier information), so the corrected value flows automatically through the feed into Merchant Center (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0727.024].
- For a missing identifier warning (older, Source A 2023):
  1. Check that every product and every variant has a unique SKU [L0855.176].
  2. Resubmit the existing product feed so the products are pulled in again. Do not create a new feed [L0855.176].
  3. Wait a couple of days for the missing-identifier warning to clear [L0855.176].
  4. If the warning remains, set the identifier-exists attribute to false for those products, accepting that they may show in fewer searches [L0855.176].

#### Images

- Promotional overlay on the image and low image quality are image issues. Use an image without promotional overlays and replace low-quality images with a sharper, clearer image [L0727.030, older 2021-22].
- A product photo can be wrongly flagged for partial nudity under Google's personalized advertising policy. If you review the images and none show nudity, submit a review request with the compliance confirmation ticked (older, Source B 2021-22) [L1170.046].

#### Limited Discoverability

Fix a limited discoverability warning (older, Source A 2023):
1. Open the links in the warning, such as the editorial and professional requirements policy [L0470.058].
2. Check that the website domain matches the domain listed in the upload [L0470.058].
3. Remove broken links and any placeholder content [L0470.058].
4. Make sure the whole store works, then submit the review again [L0470.058].
5. Have someone outside the business click through the store as a customer and report anything that looks untrustworthy [L0470.058].

Basic policy compliance for free listings (older, Source B 2021-22): the company's physical address, email, phone number and terms and conditions should be easy to find on the website. The product data should contain only products that Google supports [L0731.034].

#### Adult Content and Nudity Flags

- If Google flags products for adult content by mistake, appeal immediately in Merchant Center. The initial flag is automated and a person reviews the product only after you request a review (Source A 2024) [L0471.047].
- A policy flag on one product, such as an image wrongly marked for partial nudity in personalized ads, suspends only that product (older, Source B 2021-22) [L1170.052].
- A mismatch between prices, taxes or shipping shown at checkout and those in the feed can suspend the entire product feed, so checkout settings must match the feed exactly (older, Source B 2021-22) [L1170.052].

#### Titles, Descriptions and Other Fields

- Common disapproval causes include missing product microdata and overly long product titles. Shorten and simplify titles, and fill in every field Google requests, because fixing these errors makes Google prefer the products more (Source A) [L0732.018].
- Fix a 'product has one missing or invalid field' Merchant Center error (Source A 2024):
  1. Open Merchant Center > Products > Diagnostics for the specific issue [L0971.064].
  2. Open the product in the feed and check each section for empty fields [L0971.064].
  3. Compare a rejected product with an approved one side by side [L0971.064].
  4. Fix errors and resubmit [L0971.064].
  5. Alternatively, remove unwanted products from the Google Shopping feed app and submit a new feed [L0971.064].
- Missing required product information can stop listings from qualifying for badges such as the 30-day return badge (Source A 2023) [L0970.118].

#### Policy Violations on a Product

- Fix a policy violation (Source A 2022). When one product is flagged while identical product sizes are approved:
  1. Open the product's violation link to see which policy is cited [L0429.052].
  2. Compare the flagged product page with the approved pages side by side in separate tabs [L0429.052].
  3. Remove the product from the product feed, resubmit the feed, add the product back and resubmit again [L0429.052].
- Find the cause of a violation (Source A 2023):
  1. Note whether the violation appears in Google Merchant Center or in Google Ads [L0855.178].
  2. Copy the exact warning wording, because the wording shows which policy is involved [L0855.178].
  3. Find the flagged text or image on the product page and read the policy that the warning names [L0855.178].
  4. Change the flagged content, then resubmit the product or request a review [L0855.178].
- Product pages flagged as unsupported shopping content or limited can be checked against competitor pages that sell the same product without a warning. Compare the description for copied supplier text or unique wording that might trigger the flag, and do not copy competitor text (Source A 2025) [L0472.018].
- A product disapproval for a dangerous or prohibited category can be a false positive from automated review, for example a steam shower flagged as recreational drug equipment. Check the product's category and content before accepting the disapproval as correct (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0730.013].
- A disapproved product's detail page has an Actions section that suggests reviewing the Shopping ads policies and updating the feed to meet requirements, with a Learn more link. Use Request review only when the product is actually compliant. If it breaks a policy, fix the feed data first (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0730.027].
- Google's automated product checks can make mistakes. Wrongly flagged products should be challenged with a review request, while real product errors should be fixed in Shopify and the feed (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0727.023].

### Manual Reviews and Appeals

- Review a disapproved product (older, Source B 2021-22):
  1. Open Diagnostics > View examples for the issue, click the product, and check the item status [L0727.019].
  2. If the product is wrongly flagged (for example, a steam shower wrongly flagged as recreational drugs or drug-related equipment), select Request review [L0727.019].
  3. Tick the box confirming the product complies with Shopping ads policies and the product feed specification [L0727.019].
  4. Submit the manual review request [L0727.019].
  5. Review takes about one day, and the product is expected to be reapproved within 24 hours [L0727.019, L0727.032].
- Request a manual review for a wrongly disapproved product (older, Source B 2021-22):
  1. Open Products > All products and click the product, then find the issue in the Item status section [L0730.014].
  2. Under Actions, click Request review [L0730.014].
  3. Tick the confirmation box that the product complies with Shopping ads policies and the product feed specification [L0730.014].
  4. Click to request the manual review [L0730.014].
  5. Wait. The status changes to under review and a person reviews the product. Re-approval is expected within up to 24 hours, after which the product returns to the feed and can be advertised [L0730.014].
  6. While under review, no other action is possible on that product [L0730.014].
- A product under manual review cannot be edited or acted on further until Google decides, so fix all other issues on that product before requesting a review (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0727.032].
- Use Request review only when the product is actually compliant [L0730.027, older 2021-22].
- If a Google Merchant Center account or product listing is disapproved or suspended, request a review through Merchant Center. Follow the Google support document on requesting a GMC review, which describes the submission path (Source A 2023) [L1093.004].
- If the suspension looks like an algorithm error, investigate the product first and then request a review (older, Source B 2021-22):
  1. Open Products > All products [L1170.041].
  2. Search or filter for the product [L1170.041].
  3. Open the product to view its data points [L1170.041].
  4. Compare the final attributes Google uses with the raw feed attributes. Missing attributes often explain suspension [L1170.041].
  5. Check the Item status for violated policies and affected destinations [L1170.041].
  6. If the suspension looks like an algorithm error, tick the compliance confirmation and click REQUEST REVIEW [L1170.041].
- Product data changes in Merchant Center can take up to 30 minutes to appear. Diagnostics lists disabled products, but the individual product page usually gives the specific reason (older, Source B 2021-22) [L1170.042].
- When fixing a suspension or product disapproval, read Google's Shopping ads policies and the product data specification pages before you change anything. These pages are linked from the Merchant Center diagnostics and define what each issue means (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0727.033].

### Account-Level Suspensions and Country Scope

- A small share of disapproved products does not suspend the whole account. The risk of account suspension rises significantly when a large share of products is disapproved, for example 3,000 out of 6,000 (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0727.020].
- A well managed feed of about 6,000 products including variants can have a few products disapproved at any time. A share below 1 percent of affected items is not a serious problem, while a large share (for example 3,000 of 6,000) greatly raises the risk of a whole-account suspension (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0730.010].
- A high number of disapproved products relative to the total feed increases the chance of an account-wide suspension (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0730.011].
- Example from an active account (older, Source B 2021-22): about 6,000 approved products (including variants), with a few disapproved items, mostly from invalid GTIN values, missing shipping value, promotional overlay on the image and a policy violation. Less than 1% of past clicks were affected by these issues [L0727.022].
- Account-wide suspensions appear under Merchant Center > Diagnostics > Account issues. Each country where the account is suspended is listed separately, so a suspended country (for example Canada) can be inactive while the main country account stays active (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0727.021].
- Account-wide suspensions appear under Account issues, with the affected country and the reason stated. A suspension for one country (e.g. Canada) does not affect the account for another country if no products are offered there (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0730.017].
- An account-level suspension appears on the Overview as a notice that all items are suspended from listed destinations, with a reason such as a feed specification violation for inappropriate currency. The suspension can cover all destinations or only one country, for example Canada, while a store with no offers in that country stays unaffected in the other country (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0730.026].
- A feed specification violation such as an inappropriate currency can suspend the account for one destination country only, even when no products are offered there. Under Diagnostics > Account issues, each suspended country is listed separately, so check the country named in the notice and the currency set for it in the feed (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0727.031].

### Approval Timelines

The sources give different values for different situations. Each value below is paired with the situation it describes.

| Situation | Timeline | Source |
|---|---|---|
| First Merchant Center review of a clean submission (no warnings, no exclusions) | 2 to 4 days; products stay in Pending during this period | [L0182.003, L1168.006, L1168.007] |
| First Merchant Center review, sometimes longer | Up to about four days (Source A) | [L1168.007] |
| Feed moving from pending to approved after submission | 2 to 3 days | [L0964.055] |
| Merchant Center approval in general | Usually a few days, sometimes up to a week; campaigns can be set up while products are pending, but nothing spends until approval | [L0941.063] |
| Google approval and first impressions, no fixed timeline (older, 2020) | A day to about a week or more; check the account daily after launch | [L0468.117] |
| Merchant Center approval problems for a new store | About 20 days of delay (Source A 2025) | [L0667.002] |
| New Google Ads Shopping campaign under review | Status shows All ads under review; about 30 minutes or a few days; impressions and clicks should start within a day once approved | [L0743.025] |
| First-time Google Ads approval (older, 2020) | About 2 days or more; impressions start only after approval | [L1111.101] |
| Campaign stuck because of a feed issue | Delete the campaign and recreate it; approval should follow within about a day | [L0964.055] |
| Manual review of a wrongly flagged product (older, Source B 2021-22) | About one day for review; reapproval within 24 hours | [L0727.019, L0727.032, L0730.014] |

- Newly submitted products have the status Pending, which is normal. The first review by Google usually takes 2 to 4 days, and sometimes up to about four days, before products become approved [L1168.007].
- After Merchant Center approves a product, it appears in the free product listings in Google Shopping without any manual submission at the account setup stage. Until approval, the product status shows 'processing', and that label disappears once the product is approved (Source A) [L0729.019].
- In the Symprosis Google Shopping Feed dashboard, a newly linked store shows all products as Pending [L1168.014].
- If a Google Ads campaign is stuck because of a feed issue, delete the campaign and recreate it. Approval should follow within about a day [L0964.055].
- If Google gives a date by which a policy warning must be resolved, do not keep editing the product page past that date. Set the product to inactive if the warning is still not cleared (Source A 2025) [L0472.019].
- Check the account daily after launch, because there is no fixed approval timeline [L0468.117, older 2020].
- If free listings setup fails to add products on the same step for several days in a row, contact Google Merchant Center support. The cause may be a glitch or a setting that needs to be turned on (Source A 2023) [L0835.139].

### Feed Sync and Update Timing

- Once a corrected feed is submitted, Google Ads and Merchant Center resubmit about every 24 hours. Let the corrected feed resubmit to Merchant Center, which happens about every 24 hours [L1015.001].
- The feed is the source of Google Shopping listings. Keep it free of errors and warnings in Merchant Center, because a suspended or disapproved product stops appearing and traffic falls (Source A 2023) [L0934.134].
- Check the last upload date in the Feeds section to confirm the feed is refreshing [L0732.015, L0732.025].
- Fix the errors in the store or feed app, then let the feed update [L0732.015].
- Product data changes in Merchant Center can take up to 30 minutes to appear (older, Source B 2021-22) [L1170.042].
- Resubmit the existing product feed so the products are pulled in again. Do not create a new feed [L0855.176].
- Feed diagnosis (Source A 2025): diagnose the problem in this order:
  1. Log into Google Merchant Center and open 'Feed diagnostics', which is on the first page shown after login [L1015.001].
  2. Hover over the small circled-i icon next to each listed error to read its description [L1015.001].
  3. Fix the errors in Symprosis based on those descriptions [L1015.001].
  4. Let the corrected feed resubmit to Merchant Center, which happens about every 24 hours [L1015.001].
- Do not start feed troubleshooting in Symprosis, even though it can display errors, because the source of truth for feed errors is Merchant Center's Feed diagnostics. Check Merchant Center first, then correct the flagged items in Symprosis (Source A 2025) [L1015.002].
- A feed that is offline for a day or two loses those searches [L0575.005].
- Raising the ad budget does not fix a limited feed. If Google limits products because of missing data, the budget goes unspent and extra money adds no impressions (Source A 2020) [L1088.039, older].
- Free listing placement is based on the product feed, such as product name, SKU and description, matched to the search term. Optimizing product page content and feed data improves both paid and free placement (Source A 2020) [L1088.037, older].

### Free Listings and Surfaces Across Google

#### What Free Listings Are

- Google Product Listings are free product listings displayed visually in Google Shopping results, separate from text-based organic search, requiring no ad spend (Source A) [L0163.005].
- Google Merchant Center, once approved with products correctly submitted, makes them visible in the free Google Shopping section and Google Product Listings without advertising spend (Source A) [L0168.002].
- Google product listings are free product placements that appear in the Google Shopping section, separate from the normal text results of organic search (Source A) [L0586.007].
- Google Product Listings (free) let a store show its products in Google Shopping results without paid ads. They require a connected Google Merchant Center account with correct product data (Source A 2020) [L1087.005, older].
- Free product listings appear on the Shopping tab of a Google search, below the sponsored ads, at no cost per click. They require a product feed set up in Google Merchant Center (Source A 2025) [L0807.018].
- Free Google Shopping product listings cost nothing, so every product can be listed there whether or not it receives paid ad spend (Source A 2023) [L0970.118].
- Free listings in Google Shopping appear without ad spend, so low-margin products can still earn sales from them (Source A 2025) [L0966.086].
- Google Merchant Center lets products appear for free in the free section of Google Shopping and in product listings. This adds qualified traffic and sales alongside paid campaigns (Source A) [L1393.002].
- Free Google product listings give traffic without ad spend and should be used for products with thin margins. Organic traffic from Google and Bing can also reach those products (Source A 2020) [L1111.107, older].
- Free listings give no per-click cost, so they suit products that paid traffic cannot profit from (Source A 2025) [L0807.017].

#### Setup

Get free product listings on Google (Source A 2020, older):
1. Link your Shopify products to your Google Merchant Center account [L0852.059].
2. In the Merchant Center settings, enable the option called surfaces across Google [L0852.059].
3. Products will then appear in the free Google product listings section, even without a Google Ads campaign [L0852.059].
4. Create a Google Shopping campaign and select only the products you want to pay for. Products not in the campaign remain free in the listings [L0852.059].

- Enable Surfaces across Google in the Google Merchant Center account to show products in the free listings section of Google Shopping. It can be turned on during setup or changed later in the account settings (Source A 2020) [L1088.036, older].
- The same setting appears in other sources as Enable Google Product Listings in Merchant Center, so products can also appear in the free results below the paid Shopping carousel (Source A 2022) [L0963.011, older].
- Google Shopping free listings should be set up through the feed app, not through the Google sales channel's Merchant Center listing option. The Google sales channel is only used to connect the Google account and for the GA4 link (Source A 2023) [L0835.060].
- Google Shopping remains the main source of free listings. Set up the shopping feed so products appear in the free product listings as well as the paid ones (Source A 2022) [L0854.057, older].
- Merchant Center's free listings also require basic policy compliance (older, Source B 2021-22). See Limited Discoverability above [L0731.034].
- In Merchant Center, the Products section shows the full product list and marks items that are not approved for Shopping ads. The Feeds section shows the last upload date, which confirms whether each feed is still refreshing [L0732.025].

#### Where Free Listings Appear

- Products in the 'Sponsored' section of Google Shopping are paid listings, while the 'Most popular' section shows free listings. Only products included in a paid Shopping campaign spend money (Source A 2020) [L0852.060, older].
- Free listings appear below the sponsored area of Google Shopping. Use them as free listings when a store has no paid ad budget; a free listing shows the store's price and description (Source A 2023) [L0964.064].
- Google Shopping now shows free product listings below paid ads, while prominent product listing ads stay paid. Campaigns that already work should not be changed (Source A 2020) [L0967.084, older].
- Paid results sit above the gray line, while free listings appear below it (Source A 2021) [L0853.053, older].
- Google Shopping product listings appear in free listings and paid shopping. Products excluded from feeds do not appear in those placements, which is why add-on products must be left out of feeds (Source A 2023) [L1283.106].
- Some free listings on Google Shopping come from third-party marketplaces that list other sellers' products, so a competitor product link may not be sold by that store. Check the seller before assuming a competitor is a direct retailer (Source A 2023) [L1094.044].

#### Free Listings Without Paid Campaigns

- When a product is taken out of a paid Google Shopping campaign because it does not convert, it can stay in the free Google product listings. Stopping spend on a product therefore does not remove its organic Shopping visibility (Source A 2022) [L1113.083, older].
- Check Google Merchant Center for the reason a product is partially approved when free listings show zero impressions while paid ads work. If no reason is shown, contact Google support (Source A 2021) [L0968.062, older].

### Sequencing: Free Listings Before Paid Ads

1. Stage your Google integration in two phases:
   1. First, ensure all products are approved in free Google Shopping listings (2-4 days) [L0182.008].
   2. Only then set up Google Ads campaigns [L0182.008].
   3. This prevents wasting ad spend on unapproved or pending inventory and ensures a stable feed before paid traffic drives to your store [L0182.008].
2. Do not connect Google Ads to your Merchant Center account until free listings approval is fully complete. Premature Ads setup will spend budget on products still in Pending status [L0182.009].
3. Approved products first appear in the Free listings section of Google Shopping, not in paid ads. Google Ads is intentionally not linked until all products are approved in the free section [L1168.008].
4. Google Shopping products must be approved in the free Shopping listings in Google Merchant Center before a paid Shopping campaign is launched. Approval status shows there as approved, and any pending, limited, or Google-requested changes must be fixed first [L0743.001].
5. In Merchant Center, free product listings are set up first, Shopping ads (the paid program) are the main program, and Dynamic remarketing is used later. The settings carry over from free listings to paid listings (older, Source B 2021-22) [L0731.023].
6. Google ads, and products generally, start earning once approved. Nothing spends until approval [L0941.063].
7. If you do not want to start with paid ads, submit products to Google Merchant Center for free listings and build organic SEO. Move to paid ads once organic sales have built up a budget (Source A 2021) [L0671.089, L0671.226, older].
8. A new store can start with the free listings while it builds a bankroll (Source A 2024) [L0360.045].
9. Free traffic sources that can be used long term are the free Google product listings (not paid Product Listing Ads) and optimized organic results on Google. Both should be in place before relying on short-term tactics (Source A 2022) [L0429.013, older].
10. Products can be submitted to Google Merchant Center as free Google product listings, which give free traffic to product pages, or as paid Google Shopping ads (Source A 2024) [L0360.045].

Note on the two approaches: the staged approach above, which holds off linking Google Ads until free listings are approved, is the recommended path to avoid wasted spend [L0182.008, L0182.009, L1168.008]. Campaigns can be set up while products are still pending, but nothing spends until approval [L0941.063].

### Product Selection for Free and Paid Placement

- Products with thin margins can be pushed through free traffic, while products with healthy margins are the ones to fund with paid ad spend (Source A 2025) [L0807.017].
- Products with too little margin for ad spend should stay active in Google Merchant Center but should not be included in paid campaigns. Their free listings can still earn clicks from the lower Shopping section (Source A 2020) [L0967.085, older].
- Non-MAP products with thin margins can be left out of paid ads and still reach shoppers through free Google Shopping listings. This avoids competing against sellers pricing at break even (Source A) [L0941.072].
- If a product still earns margin after ad costs but shipping is too high to run paid ads, keep it on the site for organic traffic. Add it to Google Merchant Center but leave it out of the Google Shopping campaign, so it can appear in free listings (Source A 2020) [L0852.045, older].
- Show free Google product listings right away, but skip paid Shopping ads for products if competitors advertise them 50 to 100 dollars cheaper above the gray line (Source A 2021) [L0853.053, older].
- Set a one-cent cost per click for products you want to keep in free Shopping listings without funding them with ad money. Use higher cost per click bids for the few products with the biggest opportunity (Source A 2023) [L0934.127].
- To run Shopping ads with a mixed catalog (Source A 2022, older):
  1. Submit the full product feed to Google Merchant Center, including accessories [L0803.042].
  2. Run paid Product Listing Ads only for products in your target price range [L0803.042].
  3. List the lower-priced add-on products as free Google product listings, which are organic, so they get traffic without ad spend [L0803.042].
- Free listing placement and paid placement both benefit from clean product data. Products with missing data stop listing well (Source A 2020) [L1088.037, older].

#### Further details

1. Open the Merchant Center account and find the rejection reason for each product.
2. Take a screenshot showing the rejection reasons.
3. Send the screenshot and the store link to support so the cause can be pinpointed.
[L0966.085]

## Shopping Campaign Fundamentals and the Alpha-Beta Structure

### How Shopping Ads Work

- Shopping ads are paid ads that show the product image, price and store name. They appear on Google's front page and at the top of Shopping results. [L0163.006]
- Shopping ads give more control over traffic volume and scaling than any other Google traffic method. [L0163.007]
- Once created and approved, Shopping ads show product listings at the top of Google Search results. [L0168.003]
- Paid Shopping ads appear in two places: [L0186.001]
  - the top carousel on the main results page, labelled Sponsored [L0186.001]
  - the top section of the Google Shopping tab, labelled Sponsored [L0186.001]
- Anything with a Sponsored label is a paid ad. Below the paid ads are non-sponsored free listings from Google Merchant Center. [L0186.001]
- Shopping campaigns contain no keyword bidding. Optimization happens in the Google Merchant Center product feed, which has one row per product. The only text-level control in Google Ads is negative keywords. Titles, attributes and images belong in Merchant Center. [L0220.012]
- Shopping ads show for product names, SKU numbers and brand names taken from the feed, together with the product image, store name and price. Because searchers already know what they want, these clicks carry strong buying intent, provided negative keywords are set up correctly. [L0373.006]

#### Feed-Driven Matching

- The advertiser does not choose keywords. All products are submitted to Google Merchant Center, and Google reads the product data (titles, descriptions, brand, product names, SKUs) to decide which searches show the ad. [L0714.008, L0743.003, L0186.003]
- Accurate product page data therefore drives matching. [L0714.008]
- Google does not allow manually chosen keywords. Matching search terms are derived automatically from the product feed, so bid control has to come from campaign structure and negative keywords. [L0746.001]
- Google matches products to searches using feed data and its own algorithms. The levers the advertiser controls are the product data and the exclusions. [L0739.016]
- Google decides the triggering searches automatically from the supplied product data. This saves writing ads and choosing keywords. However, Google often shows products for weakly relevant searches and does not reliably judge search intent, so the advertiser has to manage this. [L0741.009]
- *(Older advice, 2019)* Google Shopping has no direct keyword targeting. The only controls are the search terms that trigger ads and the negative keywords you add. Searches that are too vague or broad usually produce few clicks. [L0357.034]
- Shopping campaigns do not use advertiser-chosen keywords the way Search campaigns do. Titles, descriptions, brand, product names and SKUs from the Shopify store are matched through Merchant Center. [L0743.003]
- Google auto-selects search terms rather than letting the advertiser choose them. A single campaign therefore cannot bid higher on high-converting terms and lower on low-converting terms. [L0055.001]

#### Why Product Listing Ads Work

- Product Listing Ads (PLAs) occupy an overwhelming percentage of the search engine results page for commercial search terms, which gives them dominant visibility. [L0046.001]
- PLAs display products visually, with images, prices and seller information, directly in the results. [L0046.002]
- PLAs are effective because they reach users who are searching to buy a specific product, meaning users in buy mode rather than in research or browsing. [L0046.003]
- PLA campaigns need no manual keyword research. Google's Product Feed system matches products to relevant commercial queries based on the product data. [L0046.004]
- Google encourages PLAs for commercial searches because they give a good user experience: relevant products with transparent pricing and visuals. [L0046.005]

### Campaign Type: Standard, Smart and Performance Max

| Campaign type | Use | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Standard Shopping | Default for the Alpha-Beta structure; full keyword-free control via negatives and priority | [L0186.006, L0742.008, L0746.019] |
| Smart Shopping | Not suitable for the funnel; no control over keywords or negatives; unsuitable for high-ticket | [L0742.008, L0742.033, L0746.019] |
| Performance Max | Not used; many clicks but very low conversions | [L0743.010] |
| Goal-optimized | Not used; removes customization and runs across Search, Display, YouTube and Gmail | [L0225.013] |

- Google promotes Smart Campaigns to increase advertiser spending quickly, not to optimize performance, because platform revenue depends on ad volume rather than on the ROI of each campaign. [L0052.001]
- To outperform competitors, use manual campaigns. They give the control over strategy, targeting and bids that simplified automated campaigns do not allow. [L0052.002]
- For a new store that is not yet receiving many orders, choose Standard Shopping rather than Smart. The course team was still testing the Smart option when this was recorded. [L0746.019]
- Smart Shopping gives no control over keywords or negative keywords and cannot build the funnel. Its spend can overshoot or undershoot, which makes it unsuitable for high-ticket products. *(Older advice, 2021-2022)* [L0742.008, L0742.033]
- *(Older advice, 2021-2022)* Google's automated campaign types, such as Smart Shopping, are reported to rarely work for high-ticket dropshipping, although they can work for other physical products. Reserve high-ticket Shopping budgets for the shopping funnel structure. [L0740.002]
- Do not use "smart" or "smart bidding" settings that remove control over individual campaign parameters. These modes stop you from separating high- and low-converting terms into campaigns with different bid strategies. [L0225.030]
- When creating the campaign, select Standard, not goal-optimized, to keep control over individual settings. [L0225.013]
- Do not use Performance Max. Choose Standard Shopping campaign at the subtype step, because the subtype cannot be changed later. [L0743.010, L0186.006]

### Campaign Creation Without Guidance

#### Choosing the Setup Path

- About 90% or more of campaigns are created without goals guidance, because this gives more bid strategy options and manual control than guided setup. [L0210.002]
- Google's guided setup pushes a single campaign type. To build an Alpha-Beta structure, choose the option to create a campaign without goals guidance. [L0454.016]
- Choose Create a campaign without goals guidance for a new campaign. Campaign goals only become useful once the store and Google account have enough sales data, which the course puts at six figures or more per month, or several hundred thousand dollars in sales. [L0746.020]
- In Google Ads, find campaigns via Campaigns, then All campaigns, and filter to Shopping campaigns. The "Go to" button at the top can be used to type "campaign" and jump to creation or viewing. [L0225.012]

#### Conversion Goals

- Keep all conversion goals listed under "Use these conversion goals for campaign performance optimization" switched on. The conversions must already be set up in Google Ads beforehand. [L0743.011]
- Leave all conversion goals enabled. [L0186.006]

#### Alpha Campaign Build (Standard Shopping)

1. In Google Ads, click Campaigns. [L0186.006]
2. Click New Campaign. [L0186.006]
3. Choose Create a campaign without guidance. [L0186.006]
4. Select campaign type: Shopping. [L0186.006]
5. Leave all conversion goals enabled. [L0186.006]
6. Select your connected Google Merchant Center account. [L0186.006]
7. Choose Standard Shopping, not Performance Max. [L0186.006]
8. Name it `Alpha, [Store Name]`. [L0186.006]
9. Set an initial daily budget. The recommended starting point is $5-$10/day total across both campaigns, with maximum recommended early-stage spend around $30/day. [L0186.006]
10. Set bid strategy: Manual CPC. [L0186.006]
11. Leave Customer acquisition on default, which bids equally for new and existing customers. [L0186.006]
12. Set Alpha campaign priority: Low. [L0186.006]
13. Find the Networks setting (very important; may be under "More settings") and turn OFF Include Google Search Partners. Conversion rates on Google Shopping are best on Google itself, not on Search Partners. [L0186.006]
14. Create one ad group named `Alpha`. [L0186.006]
15. Set the CPC bid to $0.40 (starting point). [L0186.006]
16. Keep Products set to All products included. [L0186.006]
17. Click Publish campaign. [L0186.006]
18. After publishing, subdivide products by Item ID inside the Alpha ad group for future per-product bid control. This step is optional but recommended. [L0186.006, L0186.010]

#### Beta Campaign Build (Standard Shopping)

1. Repeat the campaign creation steps: Create without guidance, select Shopping, select your Google Merchant Center account, and choose Standard Shopping. [L0186.007]
2. Name it `Beta, [Store Name]`. [L0186.007]
3. Set bid strategy: Manual CPC. [L0186.007]
4. Set the CPC bid to $0.20 (starting point; about half of Alpha). [L0186.007]
5. Set Beta campaign priority: High. [L0186.007]
6. Find the Networks setting and turn OFF Include Google Search Partners. [L0186.007]
7. Create one ad group named `Beta`. [L0186.007]
8. Keep Products set to All products included. [L0186.007]
9. Click Publish campaign. [L0186.007]

#### Alternative Campaign Builds

*(No year given)* Alpha build with a starting product shopping bid:

1. Go to Campaigns and click add new campaign. [L0225.027]
2. Select Shopping and your Merchant Center account. [L0225.027]
3. Select Standard (not goal-optimized). [L0225.027]
4. Name it `Alpha Shopping [Category] [TargetROAS]`. [L0225.027]
5. Set bidding strategy to Manual CPC. [L0225.027]
6. Set daily budget (e.g., $25). [L0225.027]
7. Set campaign priority to Low. [L0225.027]
8. Leave Google search partners ON. [L0225.027]
9. Select country (e.g., United States). [L0225.027]
10. Set devices to All devices. [L0225.027]
11. Create a Product Shopping ad group with starting bid ($0.50). [L0225.027]
12. Add universal negative keywords. [L0225.027]
13. Save the campaign. [L0225.027]

*(No year given)* Beta build:

1. Repeat steps 1-3 from the alpha campaign creation. [L0225.028]
2. Name it `Beta Shopping [Category] [LowerROAS]`. [L0225.028]
3. Set bidding strategy to Manual CPC. [L0225.028]
4. Set campaign priority to High (opposite of alpha). [L0225.028]
5. Set starting bid to $0.20 (lower than alpha). [L0225.028]
6. Set target ROAS lower than alpha (e.g., 2.5x vs 3.3x). [L0225.028]
7. Add negative keywords for branded terms (e.g., "lifestyles" as phrase match) to block them from beta and funnel them to alpha. [L0225.028]
8. Add universal negative keywords. [L0225.028]
9. Save the campaign. [L0225.028]

*(Older advice, 2021-2022)* Full build in the course's Alpha and Beta order:

1. In Google Ads, go to Campaigns and click the blue New campaign button. [L0746.025]
2. Select Create a campaign without goals guidance, then select Shopping. [L0746.025]
3. Select the linked Merchant Center account and the one country you sell to (for a US store, United States). [L0746.025]
4. Select Standard Shopping campaign and click Continue. [L0746.025]
5. Name the Beta campaign (for example `beta all products shopping`) and leave Additional settings at their defaults. [L0746.025]
6. Under Bidding and budget, select Manual CPC and uncheck Enhanced CPC. [L0746.025]
7. Enter the daily budget (the same for both campaigns, for example $15 or about $20). [L0746.025]
8. Set Campaign priority to High for Beta. [L0746.025]
9. Under Targeting, keep the Google search network, uncheck Include search partners, YouTube, Gmail and Discover, and set the location to the single country. [L0746.025]
10. Set the start date to as soon as possible and leave the end date empty, then click Save and continue. [L0746.025]
11. Keep the ad group type on Product shopping and name the ad group `beta all products`. [L0746.025]
12. Enter the bid per click for Beta, for example $0.20. [L0746.025]
13. Click Save. On the ad group page, click the plus next to Add subdivision, choose Item ID, tick the box to select all products, click Continue to edit bids, then Save. [L0746.025]
14. Create the Alpha campaign the same way: name it `alpha all products shopping`, use Manual CPC with Enhanced CPC unchecked, use the same daily budget, set Campaign priority to Low, and use the same targeting, location and dates. [L0746.025]
15. For the Alpha ad group, name it `alpha all products`, enter a bid of $0.40 per click (double Beta's bid), click Save, and subdivide by Item ID the same way. [L0746.025]
16. In the Alpha campaign, open Keywords in the sidebar, click the plus next to Negative keywords, and add only universal negatives (terms that should never match, for example course and videos for a merchandise store). Then save. [L0746.025]
17. In the Beta campaign, open Keywords, click the plus next to Negative keywords, and add brand names, SKU numbers, popular product names, the strong product-name variants and the same universal negatives. Then save. [L0746.025]
18. Wait about one day for approval, then open Ads and extensions to check the approval status. Impressions and clicks can take a few days to start arriving. [L0746.025]

#### Setup Order Summary

1. Create the Alpha campaign (campaign without guidance, Shopping, Standard Shopping, a name in the style `alpha... Source A merch`, Low priority, Manual CPC, $0.40 CPC, Search Partners off, Item ID subdivision on). [L0743.020]
2. Create the Beta campaign the same way: same conversion goals, Standard Shopping, High priority, Manual CPC, $0.20 CPC, Search Partners off, country and locations as needed. [L0743.020]
3. Create a shared budget under Tools > Budgets and bidding > Shared budgets, add both campaigns, set the daily budget ($5 to $10), and save. [L0743.020]
4. Add negative keywords to the Beta campaign. [L0743.020]
5. Wait for the campaigns to be approved. [L0743.020]

### Bidding Strategy and Starting Bids

#### Bid Strategy

- Manual CPC is the bid strategy in the Alpha and Beta build procedures. [L0186.006, L0186.007, L0746.025]
- Alpha is described with the Maximize Revenue bid strategy, aggressive bids, Low priority, and negative keywords that block low-converting terms and universal negatives. This differs from the Manual CPC build steps above. [L0055.002]
- Do not use Enhanced CPC. Uncheck it under Bidding and budget. [L0746.025]

#### Starting Bids

| Campaign | Starting bid | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Alpha | $0.40 per click | [L0186.004, L0186.006, L0743.008, L0746.025] |
| Alpha (product shopping ad group) | $0.50 | [L0225.027] |
| Beta | $0.20 per click (about half of Alpha) | [L0186.004, L0186.007, L0743.008, L0746.025] |
| Beta (lower than alpha) | $0.20 | [L0225.028] |

- The starting manual CPC for Alpha is $0.40 (40 cents), to be adjusted over time. The starting CPC for Beta is half of the Alpha bid, $0.20 (20 cents). [L0743.008]
- The Beta bid is the lower of the two in every case. [L0746.007]
- The Alpha campaign gets the higher CPC bid and Beta the lower, because Alpha traffic is worth more and it is acceptable to pay more for it. [L0746.007]
- Give every product group the same starting bid, and adjust bids only once performance data has built up. Bids set on guesses before data exists tend to be wrong. [L0503.009]
- The ad group bid starts at the campaign's starting CPC. [L0743.018]

#### Target ROAS

- Alpha example: typically produces ROAS around 15x, so start with a CPC bid of $0.40. Beta example: typically produces ROAS around 8x, so start with a CPC bid of $0.20. [L0186.004]
- Target ROAS examples in alternative builds: Alpha 3.3x, Beta 2.5x (lower than alpha). [L0225.028, L0225.014]
- Target ROAS example in naming: 3.6 for a shopping campaign for cold traffic in the USA. [L0327.021]

#### Customer Acquisition and Local Settings

- Leave Customer acquisition on the default, which bids equally for new and existing customers. [L0186.006]
- Keep the default "bid equally for new and existing customers" setting, so returning customers who search for products are bid on equally. [L0743.015]
- Leave local products off unless the business has a physical retail location. Leave EU political ads off when they do not apply. [L0743.016, L0743.028]

#### Why Two Bid Levels

- Using one budget and one campaign for all keywords sets equal bids for low- and high-converting terms and reduces profitability. Splitting into two campaigns lets most of the budget go to the higher-converting terms. [L0743.009]
- With a limited budget, spend should go first to the campaign with the highest return per dollar, which is Alpha. Beta should still be profitable but receives less money because its traffic is less valuable. [L0746.005]
- The alpha-beta campaign structure solves Shopping's main limitation: you cannot pick keywords or set keyword-level bids. By splitting campaigns and using negatives to funnel, you effectively create high-bid and low-bid keyword groups, even though Google picks which searches trigger your ads. [L0225.031]

### Budgets and Shared Budgets

#### Shared Budget Procedure

To unify spending across the Alpha and Beta campaigns: [L0186.008]

1. Go to Tools, open Budgets & bidding options, and select Shared budgets. [L0186.008]
2. Set up a new shared budget by adding both campaigns to it. [L0186.008]
3. Establish your daily cap. Start with $5-$10/day, as recommended. [L0186.008]
4. One budget limit then manages spending across both campaigns. [L0186.008]

#### Daily Budget Values

| Source | Daily budget | When it applies | Source ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starting point for both campaigns together | $5-$10 per day total, maximum early spend about $30 per day | First launch, shared budget | [L0186.006, L0743.020] |
| Shared budget example | $5-$10 per day | Shared budget across both campaigns | [L0743.020, L0186.008] |
